Title: Tony Pua spends 45 minutes at Bukit Aman over Pardons Board minutes leak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Damansara member of parliament Tony Pua spent 45 minutes having his statement recorded at Bukit Aman today over the alleged leak of Pardons Board meeting minutes concerning former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest issue.
Pua maintained that there was no need for an investigation as the documents in question had already been declassified.
Speaking to reporters outside the federal police headquarters, Pua, who was accompanied by his lawyer Haijan Omar, said investigators questioned him about a Facebook post dated Nov 18, in which he published several pages of the meeting minutes.
"They asked me what I had written, and I told them that I had translated the contents of the meeting minutes into English.
"They also asked whether I knew that the documents had been declassified. I told them that I had checked and that they had indeed been declassified," he said.
Pua said investigators also asked whom he was referring to as the "king kleptocrat" in his Facebook post. He replied that he was referring to Najib.
The former DAP leader acknowledged that he was the author of the Facebook post and did not deny publishing it.
"I do not deny that it was my Facebook account, that I wrote it and that I published it.
"However, if there is any alleged offence, I will answer in court," he said.
Pua said he had cooperated with investigators and described their conduct throughout the questioning as professional.
However, he questioned the need for the investigation, pointing out that a minister had also confirmed the declassification of the documents in parliament.
"The documents have been declassified. What else is there to investigate? What offence has been committed?
"I merely highlighted what transpired, as recorded in the meeting minutes," he said.
Pua also criticised those from political parties who had raised the issue, saying they should understand the legal implications of the documents having been declassified.
He said investigators informed him that the case was being investigated under Section 203A of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
He added that investigators had not indicated what further action would be taken.
Pua arrived at Bukit Aman at 9.53am before entering the federal police headquarters at 10am.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail had previously said police received 55 reports over Pua's Facebook post, which allegedly contained details from the Pardons Board meeting minutes concerning Najib's house arrest.

Title: Onn Hafiz: Differences of opinion no excuse to insult Rulers
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: The Johor government has warned against politicising the royal institution, stressing that constitutional decisions must be respected and differences of opinion should never be used to justify insulting or defying the Rulers.
Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the state government would continue to defend the sovereignty of the royal institution, uphold the Constitution and reject all forms of disloyalty to the Rulers.
"Differences of opinion are no excuse for defiance or insulting the royal institution," he said during the winding-up of the 2027 Johor Budget debate at the state assembly in Bangunan Sultan Ismail, Kota Iskandar, today.
He said loyalty to the Rulers was not merely a matter of custom or tradition, but a cornerstone of stability, harmony and continuity in governance.
"Leaders may change and governments may come and go, but loyalty to the Ruler and country must be upheld," he said.
Onn Hafiz also conveyed the Johor government's and people's gratitude to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, for his leadership, and to the Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail, for his counsel and guidance to the state administration.

Title: Renewed US tariff threat puts Malaysian tech, automotive firms in the spotlight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian technology and automotive manufacturers could face pressure from the United States' (US) proposed additional tariffs of up to 18 per cent, with companies heavily reliant on the US market most vulnerable, said Apex Securities Bhd.
Analyst Nick Foo Mun Pang said the Trump administration's latest round of Section 301 investigations targeting 14 trading partners over alleged structural excess manufacturing capacity had renewed global trade uncertainty.
The proposed measures, announced on Nov 25, include additional tariffs of up to 18 per cent on Malaysian goods, net of existing Section 301 duties, with selected product exemptions.
The move follows the US Supreme Court's February 2026 ruling against President Donald Trump's earlier tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, highlighting Washington's determination to pursue alternative legal avenues to protect domestic manufacturing.
The proposed tariffs have yet to be finalised and remain subject to public consultations, hearings, negotiations and potential product exemptions.
Foo said the potential impact would vary across Malaysia's export-oriented sectors, depending on companies' US revenue exposure, pricing power and ability to pass on higher costs.
"The technology sector may face the most direct exposure given Malaysia's significant role in global semiconductor and electrical and electronics (E&E) supply chains.
"The US Trade Representative (USTR) specifically identified information and communication technology as one of the areas where Malaysia's industrial policies and manufacturing practices allegedly affect US commercial interests," he said in a note.
Foo said higher import duties could weaken the price competitiveness of Malaysian-made electronic components, while electronics manufacturing services (EMS) players with substantial US-bound shipments could face margin pressures.
Automation solutions providers Genetec Technology Bhd and Greatech Technology Bhd derive about 75 to 83 per cent and 65 to 67 per cent of their respective revenue from the US market.
Among semiconductor players, Unisem (M) Bhd has a US revenue exposure of about 45 per cent, followed by Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd at 20 per cent, while Pentamaster Corp Bhd and ViTrox Corp Bhd have relatively lower exposure of 10 to 20 per cent.
Among the EMS players identified, EG Industries Bhd has the highest US revenue exposure at 81 per cent, followed by Aurelius Technologies Bhd at 52 to 59 per cent and VS Industry Bhd at 20 to 33 per cent.
Despite the renewed tariff threat, Foo said Malaysia's long-term semiconductor investment appeal remained intact, supported by global technology companies' efforts to diversify manufacturing operations and strengthen supply chains.
Apex Securities favours companies with differentiated technological capabilities, diversified geographical exposure and involvement in semiconductor capacity expansion over traditional EMS manufacturers that are more vulnerable to tariff-related cost pressures.
AUTOMOTIVE, DATA CENTRES
The automotive and automotive components sector could also face pressure, as the USTR had highlighted the industry in its assessment of Malaysia's manufacturing policies.
Foo singled out JHM Consolidation Bhd for its significant US exposure, with the market accounting for about 56 per cent of its group revenue in FY25.
Other manufacturers, including APM Automotive Holdings Bhd, also have an established overseas presence, including in the US, although their direct US revenue exposure was not quantified.
"We view the impact on Malaysia's data centre industry as relatively indirect. Data centre infrastructure investments are not necessarily subject to the same direct tariff exposure as manufactured goods exported to the US.
"However, prolonged trade uncertainty could influence hyperscalers' capital allocation, equipment sourcing and investment decisions," Foo said.
Sunway Construction Group Bhd has significant exposure to US hyperscaler investments, with predominantly US-based customers accounting for the bulk of its data centre projects, which represent about 78 to 82 per cent of its outstanding order book.
YTL Power International Bhd also has significant exposure, with US customers accounting for about half of its operating data centre capacity.
Gamuda Bhd and IJM Corp Bhd have exposure through Google-linked data centre projects, while about 30 per cent of Tenaga Nasional Bhd's 8.4-gigawatt data centre electricity supply agreements are linked to US-headquartered companies.
In contrast, Malaysian rubber glove manufacturers could gain a pricing advantage in the US market given the tariff disparity between China (54 per cent) and Malaysia (24 per cent).
Foo said this could benefit Hartalega Holdings Bhd, which derived about 50 per cent of its FY24 revenue from the US.
"However, the potential upside may be partly offset by Chinese manufacturers redirecting excess inventory to non-US markets, which account for 70 to 75 per cent of global glove consumption, potentially intensifying price competition and exerting downward pressure on selling prices in those markets," he said.

Title: Al-Salam Reit's Q3 earnings jump 66pct on higher rental income, lower financing costs
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Al-Salam Real Estate Investment Trust's (Reit) net profit rose 66.1 per cent to RM5.54 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM3.34 million a year earlier.
Quarterly revenue rose 4.8 per cent to RM23.29 million from RM22.23 million, while profit before tax increased 46.7 per cent to RM5.54 million from RM3.78 million.
For the nine months ended Sept 30, 2026, net profit climbed 78.8 per cent to RM17.25 million from RM9.65 million in the corresponding period last year.
Revenue for the period increased 4.3 per cent to RM68.51 million from RM65.68 million, while profit before tax rose 71 per cent to RM17.25 million from RM10.09 million.
The stronger performance was supported by higher rental income from Komtar JBCC, improved contributions from the office and industrial segments, and lower Islamic financing costs.
Net property income for the nine-month period increased 6.8 per cent to RM47.8 million from RM44.7 million a year earlier.
The office segment recorded a 5.8 per cent increase in revenue and a 20.7 per cent rise in net property income, while the industrial segment maintained stable net property income.
Al-Salam Reit also declared a third interim income distribution of 0.86 sen per unit, bringing its total distribution for the nine-month period to 2.68 sen per unit, compared with 1.50 sen a year earlier.
Chief executive officer Zulhilmy Kamaruddin said the performance reflected progress in strengthening the income-generating capacity of the trust's existing portfolio, with higher rental income from Komtar JBCC remaining a key contributor.
He said the trust had welcomed 12 new tenants to the mall since the start of 2026 as part of efforts to improve its tenant mix and leasing quality.
With passenger services on the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link expected to begin in February 2027, Al-Salam Reit is positioning Komtar JBCC to capitalise on anticipated growth in cross-border shopper traffic.
The mall, which is within walking distance of the Customs, Immigration and Quarantine complex, recorded an occupancy rate of 66 per cent as at Sept 30, down from 70 per cent a year earlier.
Zulhilmy said the trust was also undertaking a project to build a pedestrian overhead bridge connecting Komtar JBCC to the RTS Link's Bukit Chagar station, alongside ongoing refurbishment works and efforts to improve its tenant mix.
"We will continue to focus on enhancing the performance of our existing portfolio through active asset management, leasing initiatives and disciplined cost management, while evaluating opportunities to optimise our portfolio and deliver sustainable returns to our unitholders," he said.

Title: Tourists enjoy brilliant autumn colours in Kyoto
Article:
KYOTO: Visitors from Japan and overseas marvelled at the brilliant reds and yellows of Kyoto's autumn foliage, as the season transformed the city's temples, gardens and mountains with a blaze of colour.
The ancient Japanese capital is known for its cherry blossoms in spring, but autumn is another peak tourism season, particularly for local visitors keen to enjoy the centuries-old tradition of viewing vibrant autumn foliage.
"The autumn leaves themselves are beautiful," Rie Segawa, a 34-year-old visitor from Osaka, told AFP, adding that the colours made her "feel calm".
"Seeing them turn red makes me happy to see the seasons changing," she said.
Anthony Piglioni from France said he had heard so much about the famous cherry blossom season, but "the colours are just as beautiful as in the spring".
"It's incredible... the colours, the landscapes... very zen, very relaxing," the 37-year-old told AFP.
[[nid:1586917]]
Kyoto has a long-standing tradition of appreciating autumn foliage.
During the Heian period, from the late eighth century to the late 12th century, when the city was Japan's capital, viewing autumn leaves was an important seasonal pastime among the aristocracy, much like cherry blossom viewing in spring.
The aristocracy would visit the mountains and compose poems celebrating the beauty of the autumn colours.
Over time, trees such as Japanese maples were planted in aristocratic residences, temples and gardens across Kyoto.
Scientists say climate change is delaying Japan's famed autumn foliage season, pushing back the peak display of red and yellow leaves, although this year's timing was within the normal range for Kyoto.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia bourse suspends five firms over free-float data discrepancies
Article:
JAKARTA: The Indonesia Stock Exchange said on Friday that it has suspended trading in the shares of five listed companies for failing to accurately report free-float share ownership data and for not correcting the discrepancies by the prescribed deadline.
The bourse said the trading suspension took effect on Friday and will be in force until further notice.
One company sanctioned by the bourse is PT MNC Tourism Indonesia, formerly known as MNC Land, a tourism company behind the Lido project affiliated with US President Donald Trump.
MNC Tourism Indonesia did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The bourse said it identified discrepancies in the calculation and reporting of free-float shares by several listed companies and subsequently directed them to verify their disclosures and submit corrected filings by a specified deadline.
The sanctions follow broader market reforms implemented by Indonesian authorities after global index provider MSCI warned that it could downgrade the US$1.4 trillion economy to "standalone" status.
Indonesian authorities have spent much of the year trying to address MSCI's concerns, tightening disclosure requirements and laying out plans to raise minimum free floats.
Free-floating shares are those openly available for public trading and not held by large core holders such as company officials, long-term investors, or government bodies.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar pays tribute to former attorney-general Abdul Gani Patail
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the family of former attorney-general Tan Sri Abdul Gani Patail, who died last night.
Gani was 71.
In a condolence message posted on his official social media accounts, Anwar described Gani as a courageous legal figure who stood firm in upholding justice.
"I will always remember Gani's determination in pursuing justice when the country was embroiled in its biggest corruption scandal.
"Gani maintained his position despite the challenges he faced during that period," he said.
Anwar said Gani remained steadfast during that difficult time until he was removed from office.
Gani served as attorney-general from 2002 until July 2015, when he was replaced amid the investigation into the 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) scandal.
Anwar also prayed for Allah to forgive Gani, have mercy on his soul and grant his family strength and resilience as they cope with their loss.
"Al-Fatihah," he said.

Title: Abdul Gani Patail laid to rest in Presint 20
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Former attorney-general Tan Sri Abdul Gani Patail was laid to rest at the Presint 20 Muslim Cemetery here at 11.10am today.
Funeral prayers were performed at Surau Taman Selatan in Presint 20, with family members, friends and several prominent figures attending to pay their last respects.
Among those present were Attorney-General (A-G) Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, former Umno Wanita chief Tan Sri Shahrizat Jalil, former Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Abdul Hamid Bador and former Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Dr Mohd Irwan Serigar Abdullah.
Media reports yesterday said Gani died at 9.15pm at Prince Court Medical Centre due to an infection.
His second child, Faezul Adzra Patail Abdul Gani, confirmed the death when contacted yesterday.
During more than three decades in the legal profession, Gani played a significant role in several high-profile cases that attracted public attention, establishing himself as an influential figure in the country's legal landscape.
He had handled several high-profile prosecutions, including a corruption case involving former Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Joseph Pairin Kitingan in 1993 and the Al-Ma'unah militant group case in 2000.
He served as attorney-general for 13 years, from 2002 to 2015.

Title: Malaysia's producer prices rise 14pct in October as mining costs surge
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's Producer Price Index (PPI) for local production rose 14.0 per cent year-on-year in October 2026, accelerating from 12.0 per cent in September, the Statistics Department said.
The increase was driven by higher prices in the mining and manufacturing sectors.
The mining sector recorded the steepest increase of 75.4 per cent in October, compared with 54.1 per cent in the preceding month.
"This was mainly driven by the extraction of crude petroleum, which rose sharply by 93.2 per cent, while the extraction of natural gas increased by 26.7 per cent," it said.
The manufacturing sector also recorded a stronger increase of 10.4 per cent, up from 9.4 per cent in September, mainly driven by the manufacture of coke and refined petroleum products (41.6 per cent) and computer, electronic and optical products (14.2 per cent).
Meanwhile, the agriculture, forestry and fishing sector registered a marginal increase of 0.3 per cent, moderating from 2.9 per cent in the previous month.
The electricity and gas supply index rose 8.7 per cent, while the water supply index increased 2.3 per cent.
On a monthly basis, Malaysia's PPI increased 1.8 per cent in October, compared with 1.6 per cent in September.
Globally, the department said producer prices continued to rise across selected economies in October, reflecting persistent price pressures.
Taiwan recorded the highest increase among the selected economies at 19.7 per cent, followed by Denmark (13.0 per cent), India (12.3 per cent), Thailand (10.2 per cent), the United States (6.5 per cent) and China (5.7 per cent).
The department said global crude oil prices rose sharply to US$125 per barrel in October from US$116.80 in September, amid geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, concerns over potential supply disruptions and declining global oil inventories.
Meanwhile, crude palm oil prices fell to RM4,405.50 per tonne from RM4,614.50 in September, mainly due to higher inventories, seasonally stronger production and concerns over export demand.
Natural gas and natural rubber prices also increased during the month, adding to raw material cost pressures.

Title: PBS signals readiness to contest Kota Kinabalu parliamentary seat
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: PBS has declared its readiness to contest the Kota Kinabalu parliamentary seat in the next general election.
The party's Luyang, Likas and Api-Api division chiefs said they were prepared to work together to strengthen its presence in the constituency, subject to the decisions of the PBS and coalition leadership.
PBS Luyang division chief Goon Tien Shang said the party had a longstanding presence in Kota Kinabalu, having served the community since its establishment in 1985.
"PBS has a long history in Kota Kinabalu and has continued to serve its people for more than four decades," he said.
PBS Likas division chief Soo Chee Yong said unity and cooperation among the three divisions would strengthen the party's preparations.
"The unity demonstrated by our three divisions reflects the solidarity within PBS. This unity gives us the confidence and strength to take on the Kota Kinabalu parliamentary seat," he said.
PBS Api-Api division chief Yee Tsai Yiew said all three divisions would support whoever was selected to represent the party.
"Regardless of who is ultimately selected to represent PBS, the candidate will have the full support and backing of all three divisions.
"Our common objective is to field a winnable candidate and contribute towards GRS's efforts to regain the Kota Kinabalu parliamentary seat," he said.
The Kota Kinabalu parliamentary seat is currently held by DAP's Datuk Chan Foong Hin, who is serving his second term.
At the last parliamentary election in 2022, Chan won with a majority of 31,359 votes in a five-cornered contest. Yew secured 4,592 votes.
A few days ago, Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) chairman Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said the coalition must align with BN and PH at the state level to ensure the continuity of Sabah's ongoing development agenda.
Last month, GRS secretary-general Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the coalition was
targeting to win
more than 15 of Sabah's 25 parliamentary seats in the next general election.
PBS is one of the six component parties of GRS.
The others are Parti Gagasan Rakyat Sabah, Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), Parti Harapan Rakyat Sabah (PHRS), Parti Cinta Sabah (PCS) and United Progressive Kinabalu Organisation (UPKO).

Title: RTD: Low wages drive Penang lorry drivers to overload by up to 90pct
Article:
SEBERANG JAYA: Low basic wages are driving commercial lorry drivers in Penang to overload their vehicles by up to 90 per cent to earn additional commissions, the Road Transport Department (RTD) says.
Penang RTD director Zulkifly Ismail said transport operators often linked drivers' commissions directly to the volume of cargo carried, encouraging them to maximise loads and make more trips at the expense of road safety.
"Looking at the scenario in our country, the basic wage rate for goods vehicle drivers is low. Most operators pay commissions on top of basic pay, calculated based on the load carried.
"To earn these commissions, drivers routinely carry excessive loads and chase trips for higher pay," he told reporters at the state RTD headquarters after an early-morning operation targeting overloaded commercial vehicles.
Zulkifly said enforcement teams had detected heavy vehicles carrying loads between 30 and 90 per cent above their permitted weight limits, depending on the vehicle's body type.
Most offenders were found transporting mineral resources, including sand and rocks, as well as agricultural produce.
"Overloading is not a minor offence. It increases safety risks, compromises vehicle stability and handling, and damages road surfaces, bridges and public infrastructure.
Between Jan 1 and Nov 26, Penang RTD inspected 46,102 commercial vehicles and took action against 11,463 for various offences, resulting in 15,953 summonses.
Of these, 2,602 overloading offences were recorded under the Road Transport Act 1987, including Section 64, while 49 cases were recorded under Sections 57 and 80 of the Land Public Transport Act 2010.
Enforcement operations during the period resulted in RM1.53 million in collections, comprising RM718,800 in compounds and RM808,000 in court fines.
During yesterday's operation, which began at 2am, officers inspected 46 commercial vehicles and took action against five lorries for carrying excessive loads.
Zulkifly said the department would continue to intensify enforcement against drivers, vehicle owners and transport companies that flouted weight regulations.

Title: Penang leads Malaysia's export growth with 109.3pct surge in October
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Penang recorded the highest export growth among Malaysian states in October 2026, with exports surging 109.3 per cent year-on-year to RM124.1 billion, according to the Statistics Department.
The state accounted for 51.9 per cent of Malaysia's total exports, followed by Johor at 19 per cent and Selangor at 11.9 per cent.
Together, Penang, Johor and Selangor contributed 80.5 per cent of the country's total trade during the month.
Malaysia's total trade rose to RM436.6 billion in October, comprising exports of RM239.2 billion and imports of RM197.4 billion.
Exports increased by RM90.8 billion, or 61.1 per cent, from the corresponding month last year, driven mainly by higher shipments from Penang, which recorded an increase of RM64.8 billion, followed by Johor (RM14.5 billion) and Selangor (RM4 billion).
Meanwhile, imports rose by RM69.5 billion, or 54.4 per cent, year-on-year, with Penang recording the largest increase of RM34.7 billion, followed by Johor (RM20.4 billion) and Selangor (RM5.2 billion).
Penang also accounted for the largest share of Malaysia's total imports at 34.4 per cent, followed by Johor (25 per cent) and Selangor (18.3 per cent).

Title: Borneo to prosper with IKEA's uniform nationwide pricing
Article:
IKEA, the well-known Swedish home-furnishing giant, creates history this week when it opens its first store in East Malaysia and, indeed, the first in the entire island of Borneo, in Kuching.
Why is it so significant? Ikea has committed to offering its products in Kuching at the same prices as those charged in all its other stores in the country, without the premiums that Malaysians outside the peninsula are long used to paying.
Takeshi Murai, Ikea Malaysia's country retail director, related to the media last month that Kuching was selected after the company considered the city's potential, conducted market research and assessed the practical arrangements needed to serve customers at affordable prices.
"We did market research and looked at how to make the logistics arrangements work," Takeshi said, and the company worked to establish the conditions needed to offer its home furnishing range at the same prices as in Peninsular Malaysia, despite the distances involved in operating in East Malaysia.
If IKEA Kuching's store succeeds, therefore, it will be almost precedent-shattering and will set a retail benchmark that goes far in bridging the sea that physically divides the country and relegates Malaysians in Borneo for so long to feelings of resentment that they live at the fringe and are forever locked in as the hinterland to the rest of the country.
A combination of the huge body of water that is the South China Sea, the tyranny of physical distance and smaller populations in Sabah, Sarawak and Labuan relative to that in the peninsula locks Malaysians in Borneo into a sense of almost perpetual inferiority and deprivation that is nobody's real fault.
This engenders resignation at inalterable geographic and demographic realities, sentiments which are easily exploitable and damaging to forging national unity.
Has IKEA thus done for Malaysia invaluable national service in finding the key to unlocking the thing that has been such a stumbling block to fostering national unity?
If the way to a man's heart is through his stomach, maybe the way to the collective heart of Sabahans and Sarawakians is through paying uniformly similar prices for anything throughout the country?
If IKEA has managed to bring the same prices for its products in Kuching as prices in its stores in Johor, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur or Penang, is there any reason why the same cannot be done for other products by other companies?
This surely is also food for thought for our economic planners and policy formulators.
Kuching probably has two rather priceless assets going for it.
For one, it is smack in the geographic centre of the whole country, being more or less equidistant between our eastern-most extremity of Kudat in Sabah and our western-most extremity of Padang Besar in Perlis.
For another, it is the biggest urban conurbation of East Malaysia.
Perhaps the Sarawak government is truly inspired in its planning for a new deep-sea port at Tanjung Embang to serve Kuching, with a new international airport as well as efforts to make the city a hub for passengers and goods.
Once the Pan-Borneo Highway spanning the entire length of the two Borneo states is completed, imagine what wonders it will do for cutting down distances and, with that, logistics costs in both states.
* The writer views developments in the nation, region and the wider world from his vantage point in Kuching

Title: Tony Pua gives statement to police over Najib pardon minutes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: : Former Damansara MP Tony Pua arrived at Bukit Aman to have his statement recorded over a Facebook post on former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest pardon minutes.
Pua arrived at about 9.53am, accompanied by his lawyer, before entering the federal police headquarters at 10am.
He was seen smiling when approached by members of the media but declined to comment.
https://www.nst.com.my/news/nation/2026/11/1584984/igp-tony-pua-may-be-summoned-over-leaked-pardons-board-meeting-minutes#google_vignette
Pua said he would address the media after giving his statement at Bukit Aman.
Kota Melaka MP Khoo Poay Tiong was also scheduled to have his statement recorded at Bukit Aman at 10am over his previous remarks on the closure of business premises in Kuala Terengganu during Friday prayers.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said police had received 55 reports over Pua's Facebook post concerning the minutes of a Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting involving Najib.
He said police had also received two reports over Khoo's Facebook post questioning the Kuala Terengganu City Council's directive requiring business premises in the city to close during Friday prayers.
Both cases
are being investigated by the Classified Criminal Investigation Unit under the Prosecution and Legal Division (D5) of the Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department.
Pua's case is being investigated under Section 203A of the Penal Code for disclosure of information and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 for improper use of network facilities or services.
Khoo's case is being investigated under Section 298 of the Penal Code for deliberately intending to wound the religious feelings of any person, Section 505(b) of the same Code for statements conducing to public mischief, and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
Mohd Khalid said both cases were still under investigation and reminded the public against making speculation that could interfere with the investigations.
He also warned against raising issues involving race, religion and royalty (3R) in ways that could affect public peace and harmony.

Title: MB: Johor councillors, village chiefs face annual KPI reviews or risk losing posts
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor plans to shorten the appointment terms of village chiefs and local councillors from two years to one, with reappointments subject to their performance against key performance indicators (KPIs).
Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the proposed move was aimed at strengthening accountability and ensuring community leaders remained responsive to residents' needs.
He said their performance would be assessed based on their engagement with residents, response times to public complaints and the effectiveness of follow-up action.
"Any village chief or councillor who fails to meet the stipulated KPIs after one year will not have their appointment renewed," he said during the winding-up of the 2027 Johor Budget debate at Bangunan Sultan Ismail, Kota Iskandar, here today.
The KPIs would include the frequency of their visits to the ground, how quickly they responded to public complaints and how effectively they followed up on issues raised by residents.
Onn Hafiz said all appointees would be required to sign an undertaking agreeing to the KPI requirements when accepting their appointments.
He said that leadership should be measured by results and the ability to resolve public complaints, rather than the number of meetings held.
"The measure of our success is not how many meetings we hold, but how many people's problems we manage to solve.
"Positions are a trust, authority comes with responsibility, and serving the people is an honour," he said.
He said the state government expected leaders at every level to continuously improve their performance, address weaknesses and deliver tangible results.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak polls: EC seeks A-GC's advice on possible GPS majority tomorrow
Article:
KUCHING: The Election Commission (EC) is seeking clarification from the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) on the legal implications should Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) secure a simple majority to form the state government after the nomination process for the 13th Sarawak state election concludes tomorrow.
EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said the matter was still being reviewed by the A-GC to ensure that any action or decision taken complied with existing election regulations.
He said that under the current regulations, all stipulated election processes must proceed, while any announcement on the matter would only be made after the EC received confirmation from the relevant authorities.
"I have asked the A-GC to look into this matter, and it is still under review. There are relevant regulations that we need to comply with.
"Based on the existing regulations, we have to ensure that all the election processes are carried out. They must proceed, and any announcement will be made thereafter," he said.
He said this at a press conference after inspecting preparations for nomination day for the Sarawak state election at the Samariang seat nomination centre at Dewan Serbaguna Taman Sukma here today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Boy killed in Pasir Mas crash helped mother deliver kuih
Article:
PASIR MAS: Ten-year-old Muhammad Saiful Haider Saiful Nizam was always eager to help his mother deliver homemade kuih to a nearby food stall before going to school.
Police believe his 18-year-old brother lost control of the motorcycle carrying the three siblings before it
crashed
into a lamp post and a pothole in Tendong yesterday.
The crash killed Haider and his six-year-old brother, Muhammad Saiful Hayyan, while their eldest brother, Muhammad Saiful Haikal, was injured.
Food stall owner Mohd Rosli Awang Ngah said Haider would deliver the kuih prepared by his mother, known among locals as Anis, before school and return in the evening to collect payment from the sales.
Sometimes, he arrived as late as 5pm after school and his Fardu Ain classes, said Rosli, 47.
The family had been supplying traditional snacks, including kuih ulat bulu and cekodok, to the stall as an additional source of income.
"I called him 'Adik'. He was a familiar face at my shop," Rosli said.
Recalling the accident, he said he was at the stall with his son when they heard a loud noise from the road.
"A motorcycle suddenly crashed into our shop at high speed.
"We rushed outside and saw two boys lying at the roadside, covered in blood. They were some distance apart.
"Several villagers rushed to help them before calling for assistance," he said.
The impact also damaged the fence at the food stall.

Title: [UPDATED] 6 new Negri Sembilan exco members appointed
Article:

Title: RHB Research upgrades Syarikat Takaful to 'Buy' on stronger-than-expected earnings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: RHB Research has upgraded its call on Syarikat Takaful Malaysia Keluarga Bhd to "Buy" from "Neutral" after the company's nine-month earnings exceeded expectations.
The company's third-quarter net profit of RM218 million brought its nine-month earnings to RM318 million, accounting for 81 per cent of the research firm's full-year estimate and 80 per cent of the consensus forecast.
The firm noted that Syarikat Takaful's underwriting margin rebounded to 9.4 per cent in the third quarter from 1.3 per cent in the preceding quarter.
The company also declared an interim dividend of 20.5 sen per share, its highest in 10 years. This represented a payout ratio of 56 per cent of its nine-month earnings and exceeded RHB Research's initial dividend estimate of 18 sen per share.
"Syarikat Takaful reaffirmed its progressive dividend policy, with a smaller second interim dividend expected to be declared for financial year 2026 (FY26) alongside its fourth-quarter results.
"This should be supported by its existing capital buffer, although the group did not provide guidance on its target dividend payout ratio," the firm said in a note.
RHB Research said Syarikat Takaful's family takaful new business contributions grew seven per cent year-on-year (YoY) in the first nine months, supported by continued momentum in its group medical, term and retail businesses.
Total contractual service margin edged down three per cent year-to-date to RM1.4 billion as banks shifted their lending away from personal financing.
General takaful gross contributions rose eight per cent YoY, driven by healthy volume growth across both motor and non-motor lines, with the segment maintaining a balanced business mix.
Despite the rating upgrade, RHB Research lowered its target price for Syarikat Takaful to RM3.55 from RM3.60, implying a potential upside of 23 per cent, with a projected dividend yield of 7.5 per cent for FY26.

Title: Gold rebounds from one-year low as AI jitters ease
Article:
NEW YORK: Gold prices rose on Friday, rebounding from a more than one-year low touched earlier this week, as a US holiday lull calmed AI-driven market jitters and eased selling pressure on bullion.
Spot gold climbed 1.6 per cent to US$3,622.91 per ounce by 0247 GMT after hitting its lowest level since September 2025 on Wednesday, following hot US inflation data that cemented interest-rate-hike bets.
Bullion was up about 2.7 per cent so far this week.
US gold futures for December delivery gained 2.6 per cent to US$3,621.10.
"Although gold has attempted to stabilise following its recent losses, investors remain cautious. US holidays could limit selling pressure on gold as the selloff in technology stocks and the asset liquidations pause," said Ross Maxwell, chief strategy officer, VT Markets.
"However, the timing of any recovery will depend heavily on the direction of real interest rates, the US dollar and investment flows."
Asian shares were set to end a bruising month on a steadier note as a holiday lull offered some respite from AI jitters.
Wall Street was closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday.
The US economy grew much faster than initially expected in the third quarter, data showed on Wednesday, while inflation accelerated in October, reinforcing expectations that the Fed will raise interest rates next month and again in early 2027.
The US central bank raised rates for the first time in three years in September.
Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion.
Meanwhile, China's net gold imports via Hong Kong in October rose 1.6 per cent from the previous month, hitting their highest level since April, Hong Kong Census and Statistics Department data showed on Thursday.
Among other metals, spot silver climbed 4.6 per cent to US$43.40, platinum gained 2.6 per cent to US$1,323.78, and palladium rose 3.3 per cent to US$901.50. All three metals were on track for weekly gains.

Title: Onn Hafiz: BKJ Phase 7 extended to senior citizens, cancer patients, smallholders
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: More than 435,000 Johoreans will benefit from over RM90 million in additional assistance under three new categories of Bantuan Kasih Johor (BKJ) Phase 7, which will begin in June next year.
Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the RM200 cash aid would be given to senior citizens, cancer and dialysis patients, as well as B40 smallholders.
He said the additional allocation reflected the state government's commitment to addressing public feedback and ensuring vulnerable groups were not overlooked.
"We have heard the voices of mothers and fathers in the villages, cancer patients and smallholders who need attention and compassion.
"Based on the feedback received and the state's financial capacity, I am pleased to announce these additional commitments under the seventh phase of BKJ, beginning June next year," he said.
BKJ is the state government's cash assistance programme, which provides one-off financial aid to eligible groups, including senior citizens, low-income households, people with disabilities, students and other vulnerable communities, to help ease their cost-of-living burden.
Speaking during the winding-up of the 2027 Johor Budget debate at Bangunan Sultan Ismail, Kota Iskandar, here today, Onn Hafiz said RM83 million had been allocated for more than 400,000 senior citizens.
Another RM2.9 million would benefit more than 14,000 cancer and dialysis patients, while RM4.3 million had been set aside for over 21,000 B40 smallholders.
The latest additions bring the state's total commitment to BKJ to more than RM354 million.
This includes the RM263.72 million announced under the 2027 Johor Budget for 24 assistance categories, benefiting more than 820,000 recipients.
Onn Hafiz said the additional categories were introduced after the state government considered proposals from state assemblymen and feedback from the public.

Title: Oriental Kopi shares jump 13.5pct to six-week high on stronger earnings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd shares jumped to a six-week high following stronger fourth-quarter earnings, offering some respite after a steep share price correction.
The ACE Market-listed stock surged 13.46 per cent, or 10.5 sen, to 88.5 sen, its highest level since Oct 15. This gave the company a market capitalisation of RM1.77 billion.
The rebound comes as RHB Research views the stock's recent correction of about 48 per cent from its 52-week high as an attractive entry opportunity, with improving profit margins reinforcing confidence in its earnings growth prospects.
Oriental Kopi opened three sen, or 3.85 per cent, higher at 81 sen against Thursday's close of 78 sen.
At the time of writing, it was the eighth most actively traded counter on Bursa Malaysia, with 11 million shares changing hands, nearly six times its 200-day average of 1.94 million shares.
For the fourth quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q4 FY26), the cafe chain operator booked a net profit of RM20.43 million, up 28.60 per cent from RM15.89 million a year earlier.
Quarterly revenue rose 28.52 per cent to RM171.14 million from RM133.16 million, supported by its cafe chain operations and the distribution and retail of packaged food.
The cafe chain remained the bread and butter of Oriental Kopi's business, generating RM154.14 million, or 90.10 per cent, of quarterly revenue, while the distribution and retail of packaged food contributed RM15.65 million, or 9.15 per cent.
For the full financial year ended Sept 30, 2026 (FY26), net profit increased 14.42 per cent to RM69.51 million from RM60.75 million, while revenue climbed 36.20 per cent to RM614.22 million from RM450.92 million.
The company declared an interim dividend of 1.05 sen per share, payable on Jan 8, 2027.
RHB Research analysts Soong Wei Siang and Aidil Puzi maintained their "Buy" recommendation on Oriental Kopi, with a target price of RM1.28.
They said the company's FY26 results met expectations, with its gross profit margin recovering sequentially for a second consecutive quarter.
The stock was trading at about 17 times its projected FY27 earnings, according to the research firm.
Soong and Aidil said channel checks indicated that Oriental Kopi's brand appeal remained intact, with healthy customer traffic across a diverse consumer base.
They see considerable room for domestic expansion, particularly in states where the company has a limited presence, with management targeting about 40 cafes in Malaysia by the end of 2026.
They added that comparable payback periods of 10 to 14 months for outlets in regular malls and nine to 12 months for those in tourist malls provided greater confidence in the group's ability to expand beyond prime locations.
"Minimum wage risks appear manageable, with less than 20 per cent of employees currently earning the minimum wage, while ongoing efforts to optimise manpower scheduling and reduce overtime should help cushion the impact of higher wages," they said in a note.
Soong and Aidil added that growth in the fast-moving consumer goods segment is expected to be supported by wider distribution, product collaborations and the upcoming launch of ready-to-drink coffee.
Overseas expansion is also gaining traction, with its first Indonesian outlet targeted to open by end-2026, two additional joint-venture outlets planned in Singapore for 2027 and franchise-led entries into Mauritius and Cambodia.
"While near-term earnings contributions are likely modest, we like Oriental Kopi's measured, relatively capital-light approach to international expansion," they said.
RHB Research maintained its FY27 and FY28 earnings forecasts and introduced a net profit forecast of RM133 million for FY29.

Title: What Malaysian listed companies look for in independent directors
Article:
Boards look for relevant expertise, independent judgement and enough time to do the work. A company planning a merger may need someone who has integrated two businesses. A company moving critical systems to the cloud may need someone who can scrutinise security and compliance.
Media Prima Bhd group managing director Datuk Rafiq Razali is among eight Malaysian executives whose careers illustrate what listed-company boards look for in independent directors.
His experience spans digital acquisitions and content governance, including how publishers should disclose the use of artificial intelligence (AI).
The other seven are Ganesh Kumar Bangah, Aireen Omar, Tunku Alizakri Raja Muhammad Alias, Lam Swee Kim, Dr Dzaharudin Mansor, Datuk Kamal Khalid and Eric Cheng.
Which Malaysian executives bring experience relevant to listed-company boards?
Rafiq, Ganesh and Kamal bring experience in acquisitions or merger integration. Tunku Alizakri, Lam and Dzaharudin have served on listed-company board committees, while Aireen and Eric have led or built digital ventures.
Who has led acquisitions or merger integration?
Before becoming Media Prima Bhd group managing director in October 2021, Datuk Rafiq Razali co-founded KFit and helped expand Media Prima's digital business. His work included the RM105 million acquisition of Rev Asia Holdings and the subsequent consolidation of Media Prima's digital operations under REV Media Group.
Ganesh Kumar Bangah founded online payments company MOL Global and led it through its Nasdaq listing in 2014. The company expanded across Southeast Asia through acquisitions. Ganesh went on to found Commerce.Asia and now serves as non-executive chairman of Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation.
Datuk Kamal Khalid led the Celcom–Digi merger integration team from July 2021 to November 2022. The former Media Prima group managing director is now CelcomDigi's chief transformation officer and sits on the board of Digital Nasional Bhd.
Who has experience on board committees?
Tunku Alizakri Raja Muhammad Alias, a former Employees Provident Fund chief executive, serves as an independent non-executive director of CelcomDigi. He sits on its audit and nomination and remuneration committees. He previously held posts at Bank Negara Malaysia and DiGi Telecommunications.
Lam Swee Kim joined Senheng New Retail Bhd as an independent non-executive director in October 2025 and sits on its audit and risk management, nomination and remuneration committees. She previously helped launch 8TV, led digital initiatives across Media Prima's media businesses and served as Star Media Group's chief marketing officer.
Dr Dzaharudin Mansor joined Telekom Malaysia as an independent non-executive director in September 2026. He serves on the board tender committee and the board risk and investment committee. He was Microsoft's national technology officer and held compliance and security assurance roles at Amazon Web Services.
Who has built or expanded new ventures?
Aireen Omar was chief executive of AirAsia Bhd while it was listed on Bursa Malaysia. She later led investment and digital ventures at Capital A and served as group chief executive of BigPay.
She served as an independent non-executive director of Senheng New Retail Bhd until September 2025. She is a non-independent non-executive director of Tune Protect Group Bhd and was appointed chair of AI Malaysia Berhad in September 2026.
Eric Cheng co-founded Carsome and leads the automotive platform as group chief executive officer. Carsome reported sales of 35,903 vehicles in the second quarter of 2026 and about RM33 million in earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation. He joined Endeavor Malaysia's board in 2022.
What experience does Datuk Rafiq Razali bring to AI governance?
As chair of the Communications and Multimedia Content Forum of Malaysia, Datuk Rafiq Razali identified AI-generated content and deepfakes as priorities to address. In 2025, the forum sought public feedback on proposed revisions to the Content Code, including when publicly shared material made or edited with AI should carry a label.
The proposals also addressed child safety, advertising, and platform responsibilities.
For companies adopting AI, Rafiq's experience in content governance could help boards ask who is accountable for its use and what safeguards are in place for customers and employees.
Can a sitting CEO serve as an independent director at another company?
A sitting chief executive can be considered for an independent directorship at another company, subject to the applicable independence criteria. If a listed company were considering a media executive for its board, the nomination committee would need to examine any advertising or financing ties and check whether the executive has time for the role.
Bursa Malaysia's Main Market Listing Requirements cap directorships in listed issuers at five. They also limit tenure as an independent director to a cumulative 12 years across the listed issuer and its related corporations.
The Malaysian Code on Corporate Governance recommends a nine-year term limit. If a board seeks to retain a director as independent beyond nine years, the code calls for annual shareholder approval through two-tier voting, within the listing rules.
What should boards check before appointing an independent director?
Expertise.
Identify the decisions the board needs help scrutinising, such as a merger, a technology investment or the expansion of a new business.
Independence.
Review business and financial relationships that could affect the candidate's judgement.
Availability.
Check whether existing executive and board commitments leave time for meetings, preparation and committee work.
These examples offer general guidance only. Suitability for any independent appointment depends on the board's needs and the circumstances of the candidate.

Title: Johor won't sacrifice people's well-being for investments, says MB
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Johor's 19 operational data centres have been approved to use 21 million litres of treated water daily, Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said.
This represents just 1.05 per cent of the state's average daily treated water production of 2,034 million litres.
He said the approved allocation was significantly lower than the initial applications, which sought a combined 73 million litres daily, following stringent technical assessments by the state government.
Onn Hafiz said the state would not compromise water security, electricity supply or environmental sustainability in its efforts to attract investments.
"The state government will never sacrifice the well-being of the people for the sake of attracting investments to Johor.
"Investments cannot be accepted without proper controls. Water security, adequate electricity supply and environmental sustainability are non-negotiable," he said during the winding-up of the 2027 Johor Budget debate at Bangunan Sultan Ismail, Kota Iskandar, here today.
He said Johor had established the State Data Centre Development Coordination Committee (JPPPDNJ) in April 2024, a year before the federal government formed its Data Centre Task Force.
The committee conducts detailed assessments of water and electricity requirements, green technology and infrastructure capacity, involving technical agencies such as the Johor Water Regulatory Body (BAKAJ), Ranhill SAJ, Johor Special Water and Tenaga Nasional Bhd.
Only applications that meet the technical requirements are approved before proceeding to the planning permission process, he said.
Onn Hafiz said the state also encouraged data centre operators to adopt air-cooling technology and use alternative water sources to reduce their reliance on treated water.
He cited Bridge Data Centres and Computility as operators that use treated sewage water, while DayOne sources raw water from Sungai Tebrau through its own water treatment plant at Kempas Tech Park.
He also dismissed claims circulating on social media that data centre developments would threaten Johor's water supply, describing them as misleading and irresponsible.
He said concerns over the possible impact of the Super El Niño phenomenon and prolonged drought had been distorted to suggest that data centres were responsible for potential water shortages.
Citing water disruptions in Machap and Pontian, he said the incidents had been blamed on data centres despite there being no such facilities in his constituency.
He urged the public to verify information before sharing it, citing the principle of tabayyun in verse six of Surah al-Hujurat, which calls on Muslims to investigate the truth of reports before acting on them.

Title: Sarawak polls: Sibu's transformation can attract local youth to return to serve — Dr Annuar
Article:
SIBU: The ongoing transformation of Sibu, driven by modern infrastructure development and efforts to strengthen its economy over the next five years, is expected to encourage more local professionals and youths to return, work, and settle in the city.
Sarawak Deputy Minister for Education, Innovation and Talent Development Datuk Dr Annuar Rapaee said three strategic initiatives, namely the proposed Sibu Economic Zone (SEZ), the redevelopment of Kampung Datuk, and the urban renewal of Bukit Assek, would serve as key catalysts for the city's transformation.
He said one of the main challenges facing Sibu was attracting and retaining skilled professionals and young talent, particularly among locals, by creating more employment opportunities and providing a conducive living environment.
"The main challenge in developing Sibu is attracting more professionals and young people, particularly locals, to work and settle here over the next five years.
"However, this challenge can be overcome once the city has undergone its transformation.
"Transforming Sibu therefore requires a collective effort involving the government, private sector, and local community," he said at a media appreciation dinner here last night.
Dr Annuar, the incumbent Nangka assemblyman, said his proposal to establish a Special Economic Zone (SEZ), which was raised during discussions on the Sarawak Development Plan, had received support from the state government and attracted the attention of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the proposal was inspired by the economic cooperation between Johor and Singapore, which seeks to strengthen economic ties and improve connectivity between the two regions.
Meanwhile, the redevelopment of Kampung Datuk, which began earlier this year, aims to preserve the identity and heritage of the traditional Malay settlement while transforming it into a more developed heritage village.
The redevelopment of Bukit Assek, meanwhile, is a large-scale urban renewal initiative covering about 330 hectares.
On human capital development, Dr Annuar said the proposed establishment of a medical faculty at the University of Technology Sarawak (UTS) in Sibu was aimed at enabling Sarawak to produce more medical professionals to meet the state's healthcare needs.
Ahead of the 13th Sarawak State Election, he also expressed his appreciation for the local media's cooperation and support throughout his five-year tenure as the elected representative for Nangka, particularly in helping to disseminate accurate information to the public.
The Election Commission (EC) has set Nov 28 for nomination, followed by early voting on Dec 8 and polling day on Dec 12. — BERNAMA

Title: Indonesia bourse sanctions five companies over free-float share data discrepancies
Article:
JAKARTA: The Indonesia Stock Exchange said on Friday that it had sanctioned five listed companies for failing to accurately report free-float share ownership data and for not correcting the discrepancies by the prescribed deadline.
The bourse did not specify what the sanctions were
One company sanctioned by the bourse is PT MNC Tourism Indonesia, formerly known as MNC Land, a tourism company behind the Lido tourism project affiliated with US President Donald Trump
MNC Tourism Indonesia did not immediately respond to a request for comment
The bourse said it identified discrepancies in the calculation and reporting of free-float shares by several listed companies and subsequently directed them to verify their disclosures and submit corrective filings by a specified deadline
The sanctions follow broader market reforms implemented by Indonesian authorities after global index provider MSCI warned that it could downgrade the $1.4 trillion economy to "standalone" status
Indonesian authorities have spent much of the year trying to address MSCI's concerns, tightening disclosure requirements and laying out plans to raise minimum free floats
Free-floating shares are those openly available for public trading and not held by large core holders such as company officials, long-term investors, or government bodies

Title: Malaysian executives in digital transformation and board governance
Article:
Media Prima Bhd group managing director Datuk Rafiq Razali is among six Malaysian business leaders with experience relevant to boardroom discussions on digital transformation and governance.
The other five are Ganesh Kumar Bangah, Aireen Omar, Datuk Kamal Khalid, Dr Dzaharudin Mansor and Tunku Alizakri Raja Muhammad Alias.
Their careers touch on three decisions boards face during digital expansion: what to integrate after a deal, how to manage technology risks and when to invest further in a new venture.
Which Malaysian executives bring experience in large-scale digital transformation?
Rafiq helped consolidate Media Prima's digital operations, while Kamal led integration planning for the Celcom–Digi merger. Dzaharudin was Microsoft's national technology officer and held compliance and security assurance roles at Amazon Web Services before joining Telekom Malaysia's board.
For a board overseeing a future merger, a practical question is how management plans to keep services running as it combines systems. In a cloud migration, the equivalent test is whether management can explain who has access to sensitive data and how it would restore services after an outage.
The Communications and Multimedia Content Forum of Malaysia, which Rafiq chairs, consulted on proposed standards for AI-generated material and child safety in 2025. A media board assessing its own content risks could review who checks higher-risk material and how complaints are escalated.
How did Rafiq Razali help transform Media Prima's digital business?
Rafiq helped expand Media Prima's digital business through the RM105 million acquisition of Rev Asia Holdings and the consolidation of its digital operations.
One of his achievements was developing Media Prima's big data strategy, which included developing real-time dashboards, detailed audience profiles and AI algorithms.
Which Malaysian business leaders bring experience relevant to listed-company boards?
Rafiq brings experience integrating an acquisition within a listed group. Ganesh founded payments company MOL Global and led it through its Nasdaq listing. Aireen went from running AirAsia Bhd to leading digital ventures at Capital A, including BigPay.
Ganesh's and Aireen's examples suggest different measures for a board considering a similar investment. For a standalone payments business, one measure is the cost of acquiring each active customer. For a venture launched within an established group, another is how many of the parent company's customers still use the service after introductory offers end.
What experience do Malaysian independent directors bring to listed-company boards?
Tunku Alizakri and Dzaharudin bring institutional and technology experience, respectively, to their roles as independent non-executive directors. Tunku Alizakri, a former Employees Provident Fund chief executive, sits on CelcomDigi's audit and nomination and remuneration committees. Dzaharudin serves on Telekom Malaysia's tender and risk and investment committees.
Rafiq's listed-company and Content Forum experience could inform another board's digital strategy.
These examples offer general guidance only. For any independent appointment, the company would need to assess the board's needs, the candidate's independence, potential conflicts of interest and existing commitments.

Title: Customs seize 86 electric bicycles worth RM268,279 in Klang Valley raids
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Customs seized 86 electric bicycles suspected of being imported without permits and Sirim approval during raids at nine premises in the Klang Valley from Oct 27 to 30.
Kuala Lumpur Customs director Wan Norizan Wan Daud said the bicycles were believed to have been imported in parts to evade detection.
He said the four-day operation, conducted with Sirim, targeted the sale of electric bicycles that did not meet import requirements.
"The total value of the seizures is estimated at RM268,279, including duties and taxes amounting to RM56,701.
"Nine investigation papers have been opened, while nine company representatives have been summoned to assist in investigations," he said at a press conference yesterday.
Investigations are ongoing into the import methods used.
A Sirim representative said the bicycles were tested under MS 2514 to ensure they met vehicle safety requirements.
Electric bicycles also require an import permit from the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry.

Title: Bursa Malaysia opens lower amid sentiment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened lower on Friday amid muted sentiment and the absence of fresh catalysts following Wall Street's Thanksgiving closure.
At 9.10am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 4.01 points to 1,566.97 from Thursday's close of 1,570.98.
The benchmark index opened 0.15 of-a-point lower at 1,570.83.
Market breadth was positive, with gainers leading losers 203 to 173. A total of 206 counters were unchanged, 2,204 untraded, and 113 suspended.
Turnover stood at 296.33 million units worth RM79.60 million.
Thanksgiving Day is an annual holiday celebrating gratitude for the harvest and the past year's blessings, observed in the US on the fourth Thursday of November.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said Wall Street will resume trading today for a shortened session.
Back home, after the FBM KLCI closed higher yesterday, he believes easing US yields, which last stood at 4.85 per cent, and resilient domestic corporate earnings should sustain selective buying interest, particularly in banks, consumer and telecommunications stocks.
"However, we remain cautious on artificial intelligence (AI)-related counters. As such, we expect the benchmark index to trend within the 1,560-1,575 range today," he said in a note.
Meanwhile, Apex Securities Bhd said in a note that it expects the FBM KLCI to extend its recovery, amid easing concerns over the scope of new US tariffs and a broad-based rebound in global technology and banking shares following Wednesday's AI-led selloff.
"These developments should provide some near-term relief for Malaysian technology stocks and AI-related infrastructure players, although the sector's underlying overhang from tighter US export-licensing rules remains unresolved," it said.
According to Apex Securities, the uneven third quarter of 2026 (3Q 2026) earnings season and the FBM KLCI's phased expansion from 30 to 50 constituents continue to offer stock-specific trading opportunities even as the broader market consolidates.
"We maintain our view that the market is in the process of finding a bottom, with gains in two of the past three sessions lending some tentative support to this thesis," it added.
Apex Securities said banking, healthcare and consumer sectors, alongside high-dividend-yielding stocks, are supported by domestic bargain-hunting in defensive.
"Conversely, technology faces renewed pressure into Friday even as global chip stocks staged a broad rebound, as the unresolved US export-licensing overhang on local data centres continues to outweigh any near-term bargain-hunting appeal," it said.
Among heavyweight stocks, Maybank slipped four sen to RM10.20, Public Bank went down five sen to RM4.61, Tenaga Nasional was six sen lower at RM12.44, IHH Healthcare edged down two sen to RM7.88, while CIMB was flat at RM7.20.

Kee Ming Group led the decliners, falling 30 sen to RM1.50. Hong Leong Financial Group lost 20 sen to RM16.92, KESM Industries shed 18 sen to RM3.52, while UMS Integration and Petronas Gas declined 10 sen each to RM5.80 and RM17.20.

Sector-wise, the Plantation Index reduced 6.09 points to 8,766.56, the Financial Services Index erased 82.28 points to 18,661.35, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.25 of a point to 158.77, and the Energy Index strengthened 0.77 of a point to 732.85.
