Title: Tuanku Muhriz tells new Negeri Sembilan Exco to stay within their portfolios
Article:
KUALA PILAH, Nov 27 — The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, has reminded newly appointed members of the state executive council (Exco) to remain within the scope of their respective portfolios and not overstep their authority and responsibilities.
His Royal Highness said recent events and issues should serve as lessons and guidance for all parties, particularly Exco members entrusted with the responsibility of administering the state.
“Focus your full attention on the portfolios entrusted to you and discharge your responsibilities with commitment and wisdom.
“I do not wish to see a recurrence of past events that could undermine the harmony, stability, and smooth administration of the state government,” Tuanku Muhriz said at the appointment and swearing-in ceremony for the Negeri Sembilan Exco members at Istana Besar Seri Menanti here.
Also present were Tunku Ampuan Besar Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz, and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-‘Abidin Tuanku Muhriz.
The ceremony was also attended by Undang Luak Sungei Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Datuk Muhammad Faris Johari; Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid; Undang Luak Jelebu Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi; and Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.
Tuanku Muhriz further reminded the Exco members to put the people’s interests first, uphold the highest standards of integrity and professionalism, and ensure that every decision made serves the best interests of the state and the well-being of its people.
His Royal Highness also congratulated the elected representatives appointed to the state executive council, describing their appointments as an honour that carries significant responsibilities and a great trust towards the state and its people.
He also prayed that the Menteri Besar and all Exco members would be granted the guidance, strength, and wisdom needed to discharge their responsibilities and ensure that Negeri Sembilan remains peaceful, prosperous, and progressive.
Earlier, six state assemblymen took their oaths of office as new members of the Negeri Sembilan Exco before Tuanku Muhriz.
The appointments mark a change in the composition of the state administration following recent political developments in Negeri Sembilan.
In the 16th Negeri Sembilan State Election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 18 of the 36 state seats, while Perikatan Nasional (PN) secured seven seats. — Bernama

Title: Thunderstorms could crash Sarawak’s nomination day, says MetMalaysia
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 27 — Most areas in Sarawak are expected to experience rain tomorrow, on the nomination day for the 13th Sarawak State Election.
According to a special weather forecast issued by the National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre of the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), the weather in the morning is expected to be clear in the Kuching, Serian, and Samarahan areas.
However, nine divisions — Sri Aman, Betong, Sarikei, Sibu, Mukah, Bintulu, Kapit, Miri, and Limbang — are forecast to see rain in the morning, with conditions shifting to thunderstorms across the entire state by the afternoon.
Temperatures across almost all divisions are expected to range between 24 and 34 degrees Celsius.
The public, including candidates involved in the nomination process, are advised to stay updated on weather developments and seek further information via the official MetMalaysia website at www.met.gov.my or the ‘myCuaca’ mobile application.
The Election Commission has set Dec 12 as the polling day for the 13th Sarawak State Election, with early voting scheduled for Dec 8.
For the latest news on the 13th Sarawak State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/sarawak/2026/ . — Bernama

Title: Smiling, silent, says will talk later: Tony Pua walks into Bukit Aman to explain his Najib Facebook post
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Tony Pua turned up at Bukit Aman today to answer to police over 55 reports lodged against his Facebook post on the Pardons Board minutes concerning former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest.
The former Damansara MP reached the federal police headquarters with his lawyer at about 9.53am, smiled at reporters without commenting and said he would speak after giving his statement, the New Straits Times reported.
Kota Melaka MP Khoo Poay Tiong was also due at Bukit Aman at 10am to give his statement over his own Facebook post on the closure of businesses in Kuala Terengganu during Friday prayers, but the newspaper did not indicate if he had arrived or not.
Yesterday, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said police received 55 complaints over Pua’s remarks and two over Khoo’s.
Pua is being investigated under Section 203A of the Penal Code for disclosure of information and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 for improper use of network services.
Khoo’s probe falls under Sections 298 and 505(b) of the Penal Code, covering wounding religious feelings and public mischief, as well as the same Section 233.

Title: Six new Negeri Sembilan exco members sworn in as Ismail Lasim stays on as MB
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Four Barisan Nasional (BN) assemblymen and one each from Wawasan and PAS were sworn in as Negeri Sembilan executive councillors today, more than two months after the previous 10 councillors lost their posts.
Berita Harian reported that the swearing-in ceremony took place at Istana Besar Seri Menanti in Kuala Pilah, where Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim announced the six appointments approved by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Umno’s three representatives are Kota assemblyman Suhaimi Aini, Senaling assemblyman Mohamad Qayyum Abd Jalil and Jeram Padang assemblyman Datuk Mohd Zaidy Abdul Kadir.
Repah assemblyman Koh Kim Swee of MCA takes the fourth BN seat on the council, alongside Gemas assemblyman Ridzuan Ahmad of Wawasan and Bagan Pinang assemblyman Abdul Fatah Zakaria of PAS.
The Tunku Ampuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, also attended the ceremony.
In September, the previous councillors backed a proclamation naming Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as ruler in place of Tuanku Muhriz.
Tuanku Muhriz revoked all 10 appointments on September 20, with the palace saying the councillors had breached their oaths of office.
Yesterday, after an audience with Tuanku Muhriz, Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the party would leave it to the palace to announce the outcome of their discussions on the menteri besar’s position and the exco appointments.

Title: Religious affairs minister demands apology from radio station over clip resembling Islamic prayer
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan has urged the management of a private radio station to immediately remove a viral video linking Islamic prayer (solat) to English Premier League football matches and issue a public apology to the Muslim community.
In a statement posted on Facebook today, Zulkifli also called on the radio station to issue a public apology to the Muslim community and ensure that a similar incident does not recur.
He stressed that solat is a fundamental pillar of Islam and a sacred obligation for Muslims, adding that its sanctity must be respected and should never be trivialised through jokes, cheap entertainment or parody in any form of broadcasting.
“To preserve harmony in the country’s multiracial and multi-religious society, all media practitioners and content creators are reminded to remain sensitive to religious concerns and comply with established broadcasting guidelines.
“Freedom of expression and creativity do not, under any circumstances, justify mocking religious rituals or treating fundamental aspects of faith in a manner that could provoke anger and threaten public order,” he said.
Zulkifli also urged all parties to uphold proper conduct, respect the sanctity of all religions and use media platforms as tools to educate the public and promote unity.
Recently, an 11-second video titled “Praying for Man United”, uploaded by a radio station, went viral on social media.
The clip featured two men in a radio studio performing movements resembling ruku’ (bowing) and sujud (prostration), alongside the display of the football match score between Sporting CP and Manchester United.
The video sparked widespread criticism from social media users, who said the content had crossed the boundaries of religious sensitivity and made a mockery of the sanctity of Islam. — Bernama

Title: Storms on the way: Penang tells all districts to get disaster committees ready
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 27 — Penang housing and environment executive councillor Datuk Seri Sundarajoo Somu has directed all district officers to activate their disaster management committees as forecasts warn of thunderstorms in most areas of the state tomorrow afternoon.
Sundarajoo said the Penang State Disaster Management Committee issued the directive to ensure districts could monitor flood risks and coordinate quickly with the agencies involved.
“All district officers, who chair their respective District Disaster Management Committees, have been directed to activate their committees so that preparedness measures, monitoring and inter-agency coordination can be carried out promptly and effectively,” he said in a statement today.
He said the State Disaster Management Secretariat will step up monitoring, especially at flood hotspots and other locations identified as being at risk of flooding.
“Inspections of assets and operational equipment have also been stepped up to ensure that they are in good working order and ready for deployment in the event of an emergency,” he said.
According to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecast for November 26 to 28, thunderstorms are expected in most areas of Penang in the afternoons.
Rain and thunderstorms may also occur in some areas at night.
On November 28, rain and thunderstorms are expected in some areas in the morning, with thunderstorms forecast to affect most areas in the afternoon.
Rain and thunderstorms may continue into the night.
“I wish to stress that public safety and well-being remain a priority for the state government,” Sundarajoo said.
He urged residents in low-lying areas, near rivers, along the coast and in areas frequently affected by flooding to remain vigilant and prepare in advance.
“This includes keeping important documents, medication and essential supplies ready,” he said.
He advised the public to obtain information and follow the latest weather developments and water levels through official channels, namely MetMalaysia’s myCuaca app and the Department of Irrigation and Drainage’s Public InfoBanjir portal.
He also advised the public to temporarily suspend all recreational and leisure activities involving bodies of water, including activities at rivers, beaches and water recreation areas.
He called on the public to cooperate fully with the security, rescue and disaster management agencies in any possible disaster.

Title: Ismail Lasim turns up at Seri Menanti as Negeri Sembilan exco swearing-in gets under way nearly four months into crisis
Article:
KUALA PILAH, Nov 27 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim arrived at Istana Besar Seri Menanti today for the swearing-in of the state executive council (exco), Harian Metro reported.
His vehicle was seen entering the palace grounds at 10.11am, after several vehicles carrying state assemblymen arrived from about 10am, the newspaper said.
The ceremony was expected to begin at 10.45am before the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Yesterday, Tuanku Muhriz received several BN leaders in audience at Istana Hinggap in Seremban.
They were Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi; deputy chairman and Negeri Sembilan BN chief Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan; Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki; and Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
The audience was understood to be aimed at resolving the state’s administrative crisis, which has dragged on for nearly four months, the newspaper reported.
Tuanku Muhriz had earlier revoked the appointments of the previous 10 exco members effective September 20, while Ismail stayed on as menteri besar.
The crisis deepened on November 16 when BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir announced that Ismail had resigned, which the latter denied on November 20, saying he had neither submitted nor consented to a resignation letter.
The palace has since told Ismail to show that he still commands majority support among assemblymen and to submit a list of exco members for Tuanku Muhriz’s consideration.

Title: Onn Hafiz urges Putrajaya to return 25pc of Johor’s tax revenue
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 27 — The Johor state government has made a fresh call for the return of at least 25 per cent of the tax revenue contributed to the federal administration in order to strengthen the development of local facilities.
Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said that the latest call is in line with the Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail’s royal decree and builds upon an initial request for 20 per cent that was submitted in December 2024.
He said the state government is currently assisting in the provision and upgrading of various facilities belonging to federal agencies, even though such matters do not fall under the state’s primary responsibilities.
“The assistance includes the repair of dilapidated police quarters in Muar, the upgrading of schools, support for emergency ward requirements and the temporary relocation of services for health clinics.
“If we had the means, the state government would certainly wish to allocate even more to support those that need assistance in Johor.
“However, this does not fall within the state government’s primary jurisdiction or core responsibilities,” he said while delivering his winding-up speech for the Johor Budget 2027 at the state legislative assembly in Kota Iskandar here today.
Onn Hafiz, who is also the Machap assemblyman, added that the state government has also provided assistance by covering payments for locum doctors, establishing the volunteer SV Healthcare Team, upgrading Sekolah Rintis Bangsa Johor (SRBJ) schools and carrying out repairs to police buildings, military camps and Customs, Immigration, and Quarantine (CIQ) complexes.
He further noted that this request is not new as Tunku Ismail had previously proposed that between 20 and 30 per cent of the tax revenue contributed by Johor be returned to the state.
In December 2024, the Johor government formally requested that 20 per cent of the said tax revenue be channelled back to the state, providing the state with greater fiscal space to pursue development initiatives.
The request was subsequently adjusted to at least 25 per cent, enabling the state government to plan and implement a larger number of development projects and public amenities.

Title: MACC pushes back against ‘double standard’ claims, says facts guide probes
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 27 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) today firmly denied allegations that it applies a “double standard” in its investigations, including those involving government ministries.
In a statement issued today, the MACC described the allegations as baseless, saying they did not reflect the principles of professionalism, integrity, and established procedures governing its investigations.
The commission said it had initiated an investigation on Oct 7 into expenditure related to the Rural Road Project (JALB), which involves a government ministry.
“To date, statements have been recorded from 20 witnesses from various relevant ministries and agencies to assist in the investigation.
“The investigation is ongoing, and the MACC is currently reviewing all information and evidence gathered to ensure that every aspect of the matter is investigated thoroughly,” the statement said.
The MACC acknowledged the right of all parties to express their views, criticisms, and feedback but stressed that any allegations or statements should be based on verified facts and communicated responsibly, rather than on perceptions or assumptions alone.
“The MACC wishes to emphasise that every investigation is conducted based on facts, evidence, and legal provisions, regardless of an individual’s position, rank, or background.
“The MACC remains committed to carrying out its duties professionally, independently, fairly, and transparently, while ensuring that the rule of law is consistently upheld,” the statement added.
Yesterday, media reports quoted DAP advisor Lim Guan Eng as alleging that the MACC had applied a “double standard” in its investigations into two controversies: the extension of the land lease for the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH), and RM2.1 billion in alleged excess expenditure by the Ministry of Rural and Regional Development (KKDW). — Bernama

Title: MCMC serves Google in RM600m lawsuit, says YouTube failed to curb harmful content
Article:
KULAI, Nov 27 — MCMC’s lawsuit against Google LLC over its alleged failure to tackle harmful content on YouTube has been served on the company’s Malaysian lawyers, said Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching.
She said this was MCMC’s first lawsuit against Google. The commission had previously taken legal action against Telegram.
“To my knowledge, the suit has been served on Google, on their lawyers in Malaysia,” she told reporters after the Aspirasi Madani and Year Six appreciation programme at Sekolah Kebangsaan Murni Jaya here today.
Teo said YouTube’s weak screening system forced MCMC to use its own staff to monitor and report online gambling content, when Google should have its own team to do so.
MCMC said 74,703 reports were submitted to YouTube between Jan 1 and Oct 28 this year, of which 74,569, or 99.8 per cent, concerned online gambling.
On Nov 25, MCMC announced two lawsuits against Google seeking RM600 million in total damages.
The first alleges Google failed to take reasonable steps against harmful content, including online gambling and scams.
The second concerns Papagomo’s republication of content alleged to have breached the law.
MCMC is seeking RM300 million in each suit: RM100 million in general damages, RM100 million in aggravated damages and RM100 million in exemplary damages. — Bernama

Title: Putrajaya targets algorithmic manipulation and unfair pricing in new e-Commerce Bill
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — The Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living (KPDN) is finalising an e-Commerce Bill to strengthen platform accountability and protect consumers from algorithmic manipulation and discriminatory pricing.
KPDN said the law will emphasise transparency, accountability, and fairness, and require platforms to disclose pricing information that affects consumers’ purchasing decisions clearly.
The ministry said the digital economy now needs more comprehensive regulation because platforms heavily influence product display, recommendations, rankings, and how prices and promotions are presented to consumers.
“In principle, using algorithms and dynamic pricing is not an offence. The technology can improve market efficiency and tailor offerings to demand and supply.
“However, consumer protection issues arise if consumers are not given clear pricing information, or if algorithms lead to misleading or manipulative practices, or cause unjustified price discrimination,” the ministry said in a written reply posted on the Dewan Rakyat website.
The ministry was responding to Dr V. Sivakumar (PH-Batu Gajah), who asked what steps would strengthen consumer protection against algorithms on e-commerce platforms, including pricing transparency and preventing price discrimination.
KPDN said the Consumer Protection Act 1999 (Act 599), including the Consumer Protection (Electronic Trade Transactions) Regulations 2024, currently governs online transactions, tackling misleading trade practices and false representations.
It added that anti-competitive uses of algorithms fall under the Competition Act 2010 (Act 712), enforced by the Malaysian Competition Commission (MyCC).
KPDN said algorithms that use personal data and user profiling are subject to the relevant ministry’s personal data protection framework.
“We will keep working with the relevant ministries and agencies so the country’s digital economy rules stay responsive to technology while consumer interests remain protected,” the ministry said. — Bernama

Title: Tears in court as six, including three RMAF officers, face death penalty over 96kg meth trafficking at Subang air base
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 27 — A relative wept in the courtroom today as three Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) officers and three civilians were charged with trafficking 96.2kg of suspected methamphetamine at the RMAF Subang Air Base, the New Straits Times (NST) reported.
The six arrived at the Magistrate’s Court here under heavy police escort, with armed officers in balaclavas and tactical gear, the newspaper said.
They nodded in understanding as the charge was read out before Magistrate Wan Noora Nisa Ngadirin, according to the NST and Berita Harian.
They were named as Lieutenant Amir Ariffudin Aminullah, 33; Lieutenant Muhammad Arief Fauzan Mohd Ali, 27; Captain Muhammad Amirul Faisall Rosdin, 34; Tan Sui Seng, 48; Nur Hanis Syafiqah Muhammed Amin, 28; and Afifah Amdas, 34.
They are accused of jointly trafficking the drugs at the arrival foyer of the base’s Air Movement Branch at 6.50pm on November 17, under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act read with Section 34 of the Penal Code.
If convicted, they face the death penalty or, if spared the gallows, life imprisonment and at least 15 strokes of the cane.
No pleas were recorded as the case falls under the High Court’s jurisdiction, with bail not allowed and mention set for February 23 for the submission of documents, Berita Harian reported.
The daily said Nur Hanis and Afifah have yet to be represented by lawyers.
Thirteen people, including seven RMAF personnel, were detained in operations in the Klang Valley and Labuan from November 17 to 19 over a suspected drug-smuggling syndicate using air force assets.
The arrests followed the discovery of 96.64kg of methamphetamine worth RM4.83 million during a routine inspection at the base, the NST reported.
The remaining seven suspects will face action under the Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act 1985, Federal Police Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said yesterday.

Title: Cyberbullying case ends with warning as student apologises to teenage victim
Article:
TAWAU, Nov 26 — An 18-year-old student who pleaded guilty to uploading a teenage girl’s photograph on social media with threatening captions was discharged with a warning by the Magistrate’s Court here today after personally apologising to the victim.
Magistrate Don Stiwin Malanjum made the ruling under Section 91(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 (Amendment 2016) after taking into account recommendations from the Social Welfare Department (JKM).
The court also took into account that the eldest of five siblings regretted his actions, promised not to reoffend and wanted to focus on his studies.
The court also ordered the return of RM500 bail.
According to the charge, the accused, who was 17 at the time of the offence, allegedly uploaded the photograph of the 13-year-old victim at a restaurant here at noon on April 17 under Section 507E of the Penal Code, which provides for a maximum prison term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
Based on the facts of the case, the victim’s mother received a message via WhatsApp from a friend who sent a screenshot showing her daughter’s photograph on Instagram along with several captions containing allegations of bullying and threats.
Investigations found that the accused uploaded the victim’s photograph after reading a WhatsApp group conversation claiming that a friend’s cousin had been bullied by the victim and another individual.
The boy admitted he got carried away by emotion before obtaining the victim’s photograph and uploading it to an Instagram Story through his own account with threatening captions.
Prosecuting Officer ASP Jeffery Kadison conducted the prosecution, while the accused was unrepresented. — Bernama

Title: Want Perak youths to stay in their hometowns? MB says plan first, remote working hubs later
Article:
IPOH, Nov 27 — Introducing rural remote working hub programmes to encourage youths to remain or return to their hometowns needs comprehensive study and planning, Perak Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad said today.
He was replying to Simpang Pulai assemblyman Wong Chai Yi had asked whether or not the state government plans to introduce rental incentives, rural community housing or rural remote working hubs to encourage young people to remain in or return to their hometowns.
Speaking in the Perak State Legislative Assembly, Saarani said the proposal, which could also include rental incentives and a rural community housing scheme, needed to be studied further as it involved comprehensive planning of the local economic sector.
He said the local economic landscape was the main catalyst in encouraging young people to remain in their respective villages.
“In this regard, a balanced economic landscape in the areas surrounding the New Villages should be able to provide employment opportunities and competitive wages to ensure that young people choose to remain in the New Villages.
“Only then they would not migrate to major cities such as Singapore and the Klang Valley, which offer greater income opportunities,” he said.

Title: Abdul Gani Patail, the prosecutor behind some of Malaysia’s most watched trials
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Throughout his more than three decades in the legal profession, former Attorney General Tan Sri Abdul Gani Patail played a pivotal role in several high-profile cases that captured public attention, establishing himself as a prominent figure in Malaysia’s legal landscape.
Among the high-profile prosecutions Abdul Gani handled were the corruption case involving former Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Joseph Pairin Kitingan in 1993 and the case involving the Al-Ma’unah militant group in 2000.
The Lahad Datu-born legal figure also led the prosecution team in the case involving 30 individuals, including Philippine nationals, charged with waging war against the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and involvement in various terrorism-related activities in Lahad Datu, Sabah, in 2013.
Abdul Gani, who served as Attorney General for 13 years from 2002 to 2015, died at a private hospital here tonight due to an infection.
Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, who confirmed the news of his death, also extended his condolences to Abdul Gani’s family.
“The entire Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) extends its condolences to his family and prays that Allah showers His blessings upon his soul,” Mohd Dusuki said when contacted.
Abdul Gani was also part of the prosecution team in the 2006 murder case involving Mongolian national Altantuya Shaariibuu.
He also led the prosecution of former Transport Minister Tun Dr Ling Liong Sik, who was charged in 2010 with cheating the Malaysian government in connection with the Port Klang Free Zone (PKFZ) scandal involving the RM1.08 billion purchase of land in Pulau Indah.
Abdul Gani also handled the prosecution of former Selangor Menteri Besar Dr Mohamad Khir Toyo on corruption charges relating to a property purchase.
He also led the prosecution team in the criminal breach of trust case involving RM76.4 million against former Perwaja Rolling Mill and Development Sdn Bhd managing director Tan Sri Eric Chia Eng Hock and handled the corruption case involving former Land and Cooperative Development Minister Tan Sri Kasitah Gaddam.
Born on Oct 6, 1955, Abdul Gani began his career in the Judicial and Legal Service in 1980 before serving as a deputy public prosecutor at the Attorney General’s Chambers in Tawau, Sabah, becoming the first Sabahan to hold the position following the establishment of the federal Attorney General’s office in the state.
Throughout his career, he held several key positions, including Sabah head of prosecution in 1991, head of the AGC’s Prosecution Division from Jan 16 to Oct 14, 1994, and head and adviser of its International Affairs Division from April 1, 1995, to May 31, 1997.
He subsequently served as Commissioner of Law Revision from 1997 to 2000 before returning as head of the Prosecution Division on Feb 1, 2000.
On Nov 19, 2001, Abdul Gani was appointed Malaysia’s eighth Attorney General and officially assumed office on Jan 1, 2002, making history as the first locally trained law graduate to be appointed to the position and the first Sabahan to hold one of the highest posts in the federal civil service.
The appointment marked a major milestone in his legal career, which saw him helm the country’s foremost legal institution for more than 13 years before his tenure as Attorney General was terminated on health grounds, effective July 27, 2015.
However, he continued serving as an officer in the Judicial and Legal Service until reaching the mandatory retirement age on Oct 6, 2015.
Abdul Gani also contributed his legal expertise and experience through various other roles, including as a member of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya.
He was also appointed an adjunct professor at the Faculty of Law of Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) for two years from Oct 1, 2011, and served as chairman of the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK).
On Dec 23, 2016, he was admitted as an advocate and solicitor of the High Court of Malaya. — Bernama

Title: Amir Hamzah urges public-listed firms to back RM3,400 living wage
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — The government has called on public-listed companies (PLCs) to adopt the RM3,400 living wage benchmark across their organisations.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said that fair and adequate wages would enable employees to meet their basic needs and maintain a decent standard of living. This, in turn, could lead to greater workforce stability, improved talent retention, and higher productivity.
“This is an important dimension of responsible business conduct, recognising that long-term corporate value creation must also take into account the well-being and economic security of the people who contribute to it.
“Paying a living wage is verifiable proof to investors, regulators and consumers that the social pillar of your sustainability report is backed by real conviction,” said Amir Hamzah in his speech at the National Annual Corporate Report Awards (Nacra) 2026 presentation dinner here today.
He said the government also remained committed to strengthening the institutional and policy foundations for sustainable and inclusive economic growth.
“Good governance, accountability and transparency are integral to this agenda, particularly as Malaysia seeks to move towards higher-value economic activities and strengthen its position in the global economy,” said Amir Hamzah.
He said stronger governance and reporting practices could help small and medium enterprises (SMEs) improve management discipline, assess business performance, access financing and engage more effectively with investors and business partners.
These capabilities are increasingly important as SMEs seek to expand their operations and participate in larger domestic and international value chains.
Amir Hamzah also said companies must invest in developing their workforce capabilities, particularly in data analytics, sustainability and environmental, social and governance (ESG) reporting, climate finance and digital finance.
“These competencies are important not only for meeting new reporting requirements, but also for understanding business risks, evaluating investment decisions and supporting long-term strategy,” he added.
Meanwhile, Nacra 2026 organising committee chairman Ong Chee Wai said high-quality corporate reporting was essential to building stakeholder trust, reinforcing investor confidence and supporting sustainable business growth among Malaysian companies.
“It also provides a competitive edge, helping organisations to attract investment and compete more effectively in an increasingly interconnected global economy.
“Through Nacra, we seek to recognise organisations that demonstrate these qualities and encourage continuous improvement across the corporate sector,” he said
Ong said the awards provided an opportunity for organisations to benchmark their practices against leading examples and raise the overall standard of corporate reporting in Malaysia.
Themed “Towards Accountability and Excellence”, Nacra 2026 is jointly organised by Bursa Malaysia Bhd, the Malaysian Institute of Accountants and the Malaysian Institute of Certified Public Accountants. — Bernama

Title: Blackouts and floods fail to derail Sabah’s 42,808 SPM candidates
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 27 — All 42,808 candidates sitting for the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination in Sabah since last Monday have not been affected by the electricity disruption affecting the state’s East Coast yesterday.
Sabah Education Department director Abidin Marjan said the SPM examination had proceeded smoothly so far, despite challenges posed by the power outage along Sabah’s East Coast and flooding, particularly in the interior district of Sook.
“We hope that electricity supply to the affected examination centres will be restored by tomorrow. If not, we have already prepared contingency measures to ensure that the examinations proceed smoothly.
“Most importantly, we will ensure that candidates can sit for the SPM examination comfortably and calmly, without any disruption,” he told Bernama when contacted last night.
A total of 324 examination centres have been prepared for SPM candidates in the state, with 13,291 personnel appointed to ensure the smooth and orderly management and conduct of this year’s examination.
The Sabah Education Department is also mindful of the safety and welfare of candidates and examination personnel, and has put in place an integrated response mechanism in collaboration with security and health agencies, including activating preparedness measures.
Apart from the power disruption, the department has also implemented Ops Payung to address flood risks, Ops Topeng for haze situations, Ops Gempa for natural disasters such as earthquakes, and Ops Wabak to deal with the spread of infectious diseases.
The T313 electricity transmission tower in Ranau collapsed early this morning, affecting both transmission line circuits and disrupting electricity supply to areas along Sabah’s East Coast.
Eight districts along Sabah’s East Coast experienced power disruptions after Sabah Electricity detected an incident affecting electricity transmission to the areas at 6.04am.
The Sabah State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN), in a statement this evening, said 153 people from 42 families were still taking shelter at the temporary relief centre at the SLDB Multipurpose Hall in Kampung Dalit Gana following floods that hit Sook. — Bernama

Title: Same RM1,000 lease for seven others, so why only KLSCAH? Lim Guan Eng asks MACC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Bagan MP Lim Guan Eng today accused the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) of double standards for probing the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall’s (KLSCAH) land lease extension but not seven other organisations that received the same RM1,000 premium.
The MACC yesterday questioned Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh’s political secretary Yap Yee Vonne for five hours over Putrajaya’s approval of a 99-year lease extension for KLSCAH at a nominal premium of RM1,000, down from an estimated RM4.67 million.
“Clearly there was no special treatment for KLSCAH,” Lim, who is from DAP, said, pointing to the seven organisations that Yeoh had listed as receiving the same RM1,000 premium for 99-year extensions in Kuala Lumpur.
He said the public could only conclude that the selective probe stemmed from the ministry being led by a DAP minister, unlike the Umno-led ministry that approved the seven earlier cases.
“The appearance given is that Umno can do no wrong, whilst it is ‘semua salah DAP’,” he said, with the last phrase in Malay for “everything is DAP’s fault”.
Lim said the MACC had shown no similar urgency over the Rural and Regional Development Ministry, which he has alleged overspent its allocation by RM2.1 billion between 2023 and 2025 under Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Zahid has rejected the claim, saying the RM2.1 billion is the gap between original and revised allocations rather than evidence of missing funds, while the MACC said in October that it would investigate if it received a formal complaint.
Lim said Yap was right that those with nothing to hide had nothing to fear, adding that KLSCAH, as a non-profit, had no means to bribe anyone or pay fines of RM50 million.
“Clearly there is no money trail from KLSCAH to Hannah Yeoh,” he said.
The seven organisations are Yayasan Tuanku Bainun, Pertubuhan Bakti, Majlis Kebangsaan Pertubuhan-Pertubuhan Wanita Malaysia, Majlis Kebajikan Kanak-Kanak Malaysia, Persatuan Bulan Sabit Merah Malaysia, Persatuan Keturunan Chan She Shu Yuen Kuala Lumpur & Selangor and Persatuan Badminton Malaysia.
Lim asked on what basis the MACC was investigating when there was no reason to suspect corruption, and what motive lay behind targeting Yeoh but not other Umno ministers who had approved similar leases.

Title: Temporary tower reaches Ranau as Sabah Electricity works to restore severed grid
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 27 — The components of the Emergency Restoration System (ERS) temporary tower arrived at the site of the collapsed transmission tower in Ranau this morning to restore the electricity supply line connecting Sabah’s West Coast and East Coast.
Sabah Electricity said the lorry transporting the ERS temporary tower container arrived safely at the site of transmission tower T313 at 1.07am.
“Sabah Electricity greatly appreciates your patience and sincerely regrets any inconvenience caused,” it said in a statement today.
The company also apologised for the inconvenience experienced throughout the disruption period and expressed its appreciation for customers’ patience and cooperation.
It said Sabah Electricity’s technical teams had been mobilised to carry out preparatory work before the installation of the ERS tower begins, while prioritising safety and compliance with established work procedures.
Sabah Electricity is also stepping up all efforts to expedite the restoration of electricity supply to affected consumers following the collapse of transmission tower T313 in Ranau yesterday.
The collapse of tower T313, detected at 6.04am yesterday, severed two transmission line circuits supplying electricity from Sabah’s West Coast to its East Coast, disrupting electricity supply across eight districts and affecting 153,599 registered consumers.
Members of the public can follow the latest updates via Sabah Electricity’s official Facebook page, Sabah Electricity Careline, or contact the company through its hotline at 15444, 088-515000, or WhatsApp at 019-8525427. — Bernama

Title: Croc No. 2 in a month: 10-foot female caught alive off Daro waters in Sarawak
Article:
SIBU, Nov 27 — A female crocodile measuring approximately 10 feet in length was captured alive in the waters off Kampung Sedi, Daro, yesterday.
Licensed crocodile hunter Jeffery Siew said the reptile initially broke free from a hook after being pulled onto the riverbank and attempted to escape into nearby bushes.
He said members of the team immediately moved to restrain the animal and eventually managed to subdue and capture it.
“However, while attempting to remove the hook, the crocodile suddenly broke free and tried to flee,” he said.
Siew said this was the second crocodile caught in the area this month.
On November 3, the team captured a large male crocodile measuring 5.43 metres in length and weighing more than 600kg at Kampung Sedi.
The capture attracted considerable attention.
Despite the known presence of crocodiles in the waters, Siew said local fishermen continued to venture out to fish for their livelihoods, exposing themselves to potential danger.
He urged residents, particularly those who frequently fish in the area, to remain alert to the presence of crocodiles.
The latest capture, he said, served as a reminder that the reptiles continued to inhabit the waters around Kampung Sedi. — The Borneo Post

Title: One tax authority? Not yet, says MoF as IRB, Customs stay separate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — The Ministry of Finance (MOF) said the government has no immediate plans to merge the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia (IRBM) and the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMCD) to establish a single tax authority.
The proposed restructuring is expected to improve national revenue collection efficiency, curb tax leakages and reduce compliance costs for the business community.
However, MOF said the government would continue to strengthen governance and improve tax revenue collection through both agencies, including by sharing information and conducting joint enforcement operations.
These measures would enhance efficiency and sustainability in tackling revenue leakages, it said.
“MOF also maintains close cooperation with international organisations such as the World Bank Group (WBG) to improve the country’s tax model.
“Engagement sessions are also held with local tax experts to obtain recommendations for improving national tax policies and the tax system from time to time,” it said in a written parliamentary reply published on the Dewan Rakyat website yesterday.
The ministry was responding to a question from Datuk Seri Mohd Shafie Apdal (Warisan-Semporna), who asked about the proposal to establish a single tax authority by merging IRBM and RMCD, and its potential to improve revenue collection efficiency, curb tax leakages and reduce compliance costs for businesses. — Bernama

Title: GPS could walk into 44 Sarawak seats unopposed after PKR pulls out, says DAP youth leader
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 27 — Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) could potentially win as many as 44 state seats uncontested in the 13th Sarawak Election following PKR’s withdrawal, said Jordan Soo.
The Democratic Action Party Socialist Youth Sarawak deputy chief said this would allow GPS to secure a sufficient majority to form the next state government on nomination day, before voters had even cast their ballots.
“Such a situation further underscores the importance of the opposition’s role in providing effective oversight and maintaining checks and balances in the State Legislative Assembly (DUN).
“The upcoming Sarawak election is no longer merely a contest between political parties. It represents a serious test of our democratic and electoral systems,” he said in a statement.
However, Soo did not specify which 44 constituencies GPS could potentially win uncontested.
He said political cooperation at the federal level should not be used as leverage to pressure other political parties or restrict democratic competition at the state level.
Political cooperation, he added, did not mean those in power should be exempt from scrutiny.
Maintaining political stability should not come at the expense of democratic competition or the people’s right to choose, he said.
“Regardless of the decisions made by other political parties, DAP Sarawak will remain steadfast in its commitment to checks and balances and will contest in the upcoming Sarawak election.”
Soo stressed that DAP had always upheld the principle that government power must be subject to checks and balances, with policies and administration remaining open to scrutiny.
“Preventing the excessive concentration of power and safeguarding the oversight mechanisms of the Sarawak DUN are fundamental political principles that DAP Sarawak has consistently upheld,” he added. — The Borneo Post
* Editor’s note: DUN stands for Dewan Undangan Negeri in Malay.

Title: Anwar looks to delivery after Parliament signs off on RM510b Budget 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — The passage of Budget 2027 by the Dewan Rakyat yesterday marks an important step in the Madani Government’s efforts to improve the lives of the people.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, in a Facebook post yesterday, said the budget also encompassed efforts to strengthen the country’s resilience and secure its future.
“May all the plans and initiatives outlined be implemented effectively, bring tangible benefits to the people and lay a solid foundation for building a more prosperous, equitable and harmonious Malaysia,” he said.
The Dewan Rakyat today passed the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027, which was tabled by Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, on Oct 9.
Themed ‘Reaching for the Sky, While Anchored on Our Values’, Budget 2027 outlines eight key principles, ranging from commitments to improving the lives of the people to strengthening the country’s resilience and securing its future.
The fifth budget under the Madani Government involves government allocations totalling RM459.8 billion, alongside RM25 billion in investments from government-linked investment companies (GLICs), RM11 billion in public-private investments and RM14.2 billion in investments from federal statutory bodies and Minister of Finance (Incorporated) (MOF Inc) companies.
This brings the overall size of Budget 2027 to RM510 billion, maintaining the government’s expansionary fiscal policy. — Bernama

Title: Sabah Electricity scrambles to reconnect East Coast after Ranau tower collapse, eyes Dec 2 recovery
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 27 — Sabah Electricity has set a six-day timeframe to restore the 275-kilovolt (kV) electricity transmission line to Sabah’s East Coast, targeting full grid restoration by Dec 2 after transmission tower T313 in Ranau collapsed yesterday.
The collapse of tower T313, detected at 6.04am, severed two transmission line circuits running from the West Coast to the East Coast of Sabah, disrupting electricity supply across eight districts and affecting 153,599 registered consumers.
“We are targeting a six-day period to reconnect the affected grid; it could possibly be completed even earlier,” said Sabah Electricity Chairman Datuk Saadiah Aziz at a press conference at the Sabah Electricity Headquarters last night.
Sabah Electricity activated its crisis management system immediately upon identifying the cause of the disruption, starting by clearing main traffic along the Ranau-Telupid road, which had been blocked by fallen cables spanning the route in Ranau.
The six-day period is required to allow Sabah Electricity and its contractors to transport equipment to erect temporary towers and reconnect the two affected transmission lines at a safe location near the collapsed tower.
Sabah Electricity is utilising the islanding method via local power stations, with the station in Tawau successfully supplying power while the station in Sandakan is still undergoing restoration.
Electricity supply on Sabah’s East Coast throughout the restoration period is being generated via existing power plants in Sandakan and Tawau, supported by portable or mobile generators, including for essential facilities such as hospitals, schools, and police stations.
Sabah Electricity has also merged the East Coast grid lines to boost supply capacity and limit load-shedding effects to between one and two hours, alongside implementing rotational rationing due to limited local generation capacity.
Power restoration was reported to be taking place in stages across several areas in the districts of Tawau, Semporna, Telupid, Sandakan, Lahad Datu, and Kunak throughout yesterday.
The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is coordinating telecommunications restoration in the affected districts alongside Sabah Electricity and service providers after 1,196 cellular sites were affected as of 12:52 pm and fixed lines were disrupted.
Telecommunications service providers are using generators and batteries for temporary power, deploying mobile generators and sharing generators in stages across 20 priority locations, and sharing a list of collector sites, while MCMC has provided Starlink satellite connectivity at 18 critical locations.
Sabah Electricity has also shared a list of hotspot connectivity and rationing schedules to support telecommunications continuity and restoration coordination.
Sabah Electricity also stressed that viral messages claiming a two-week power outage across the entire East Coast of Sabah are fake, apologized for the inconvenience caused to consumers, and provided hotlines 15444, 088-515000, and WhatsApp 019-8525427 for inquiries or verification.
This incident recalls an event on Sept 13, 2025, when a 275 kV electricity transmission tower in Kampung Sarapung, Penampang collapsed due to a landslide, leaving East Coast districts affected for four days. — Bernama

Title: ‘Halfway aligned?’: Judge gives Sabah AG three days to say which side it’s on in NGO’s continental shelf suit against Putrajaya
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 27 — High Court judge Datuk Alexander Siew How Wai gave the Sabah Attorney General’s Chambers three days to decide its exact position on Sabah Action Body Advocating Rights (Sabar) case against the Federal Government on the Continental Shelf.
It refused to accept what it considered as the vague “more aligned with Sabar’s position” taken by the Chamber, Thursday.
He said the state AG’s Chambers had three years to do so since Sabar filed the case in 2023.
Sabah AG Datuk Brendon Soh responded that he would file another affidavit to clarify the Sabah government’s position.
Earlier, Siew also expressed disappointment over the slow internet speed at the Court Complex in retrieving filed court documents online.
Soh had applied to include the Sabah government as an intervenor respondent “more aligned with Sabar’s position”.
Sabar is seeking the following declarations:
1. That the Continental Shelf Act 1966 and Petroleum Mining Act 1966 are inapplicable, unconstitutional, invalid, null, and void in the territory of Sabah after June 19, 2012;
2. That the territory of Sabah, following the annulment of the Proclamation of Emergency of 1969 on June 19, 2012, includes the continental shelf under the North Borneo (Alteration of Boundaries) Order in Council 1954;
3. That the Mining Ordinance 1960 remains valid in Sabah after June 19, 2012;
4. That Section 3(3) of the Territorial Seas Act 2012, which limits the territorial waters of Sabah to three nautical miles, is inapplicable, unconstitutional, invalid, and null and void in Sabah as of June 22, 2012; and
5. That the territorial waters of Sabah, following the annulment of the Proclamation of Emergency of 1969 on June 19, 2012, includes 12 nautical miles of sea under the Convention on Territorial Seas and Contiguous Zone 1958, and the North Borneo (Definition of Boundaries) Order In Council 1958.
“More aligned? Why? What does that mean? Halfway aligned? Seventy per cent aligned? Fifty-one per cent aligned?
“Which side is the Sabah government on? Is it on Sabah which is asking for these five specific declarations? Does it agree with the Federal Government that there’s no merit in Sabar’s contention?”
The judge wanted to know precisely whether the state government agreed with each of the five declarations sought by Sabar, disagreed with them, or agreed with only some of the five declarations.
“This is a court of law. We have to be very precise,” said Justice Siew.
Soh said the Sabah government supports the outcome sought.
“What we are saying is this that we may approach it from a different way as to the interpretation of the relevant constitutional provisions, statutes etc.”
Siew said the court needed to understand the proposed intervener’s position on the questions before it, before proceeding.
Sabar counsel Roland Cheng quipped that the slow internet speed could be fixed if Sabar’s Originating Summons is successful as much revenue can be earned.
Sabar filed its originating summons at the Kota Kinabalu High Court in September 2023, naming the Government of Malaysia as the sole defendant.
Its claim relies in part on the North Borneo (Alteration of Boundaries) Order in Council 1954, which extended North Borneo’s boundaries to include its continental shelf before the formation of Malaysia.
It contends that Sabah retained those territorial rights and is seeking a declaration that its territory continues to include the continental shelf under that order.
Cheng said the scale of the claim was substantial.
“If you look at the area of it, it’s bigger than the land area of Sabah,” he said as the stakes extended beyond oil and gas, highlighting potential opportunities for ocean thermal energy conversion and offshore wind power that could generate revenue and employment.
In August 2026, the apex court rejected Sabar’s bid to intervene in Sarawak’s separate natural resources and continental shelf case against the federal government.
Sabar applied to intervene in Sarawak’s case, saying the outcome could affect Sabah’s rights and laws, including: the continued application of the Continental Shelf Act 1966 and Petroleum Mining Act 1966; the validity of the North Borneo (Alteration of Boundaries) Order in Council 1954 and North Borneo (Definition of Boundaries) Order in Council 1958, which define Sabah’s territory and continental shelf; and the continued operation of Sabah’s Mining Ordinance 1960 for onshore and offshore areas after June 19, 2012. — Daily Express
* Editor’s note: The Sabah Action Body Advocating Rights (Sabar), is a Sabah-based non-partisan non-governmental group formed in 2021 to advocate for Sabah’s rights under the Malaysia Agreement 1963.

Title: Hej, Kuching! IKEA opens its first East Malaysia store at The Pines Mall today
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 27 — Sarawakians will soon be able to shop for IKEA home furnishing products locally as the Swedish retailer opens its first store in East Malaysia at The Pines Mall, Batu Kawa, today.
The opening marks a new phase in IKEA’s presence in Sarawak, which began with a collection point serving customers in the state before expanding to a physical retail outlet featuring the retailer’s first small-format store concept in Malaysia.
IKEA Kuching store manager Pathmalingam Arumugam said the 3,634-square-metre outlet would offer approximately 5,180 home furnishing articles, with prices on par with those at IKEA stores in peninsular Malaysia.
He was speaking during a media preview session hosted by emcee Daphne Iking, attended by media representatives from Sarawak and Kuala Lumpur, as well as key opinion leaders (KOLs).
Located on the first floor of The Pines Mall, the store features a showroom, Markethall, selected take-home products, an IKEA Planning Studio, IKEA for Business and a grab-and-go IKEA Food section.
Of the 5,180 articles available, about 2,400 are offered as cash-and-carry items for customers to purchase and take home immediately, while the remaining 2,780 can be ordered for home delivery.
The product range covers various areas of the home, including living rooms, bedrooms, dining spaces, kitchens, storage and children’s rooms.
Shoppers can also explore seven room settings and 31 home furnishing inspirations, featuring practical ideas and solutions for different living spaces.
For customers planning home improvements, the store offers assistance with kitchen, wardrobe and storage solutions through its planning services.
Its IKEA for Business service also provides furnishing solutions for businesses of different sizes.
Meanwhile, the IKEA Food section will offer grab-and-go Swedish favourites, including meatballs in a cup, curry puffs and chicken sausage buns.
Customers who prefer online shopping can browse IKEA’s range of more than 5,000 home furnishing articles through its website, with delivery and collection options subject to product availability and address eligibility.
Home deliveries within Kuching are expected to take about two to three days, while deliveries to locations outside the city, including Sibu, Miri, Bintulu and Kota Kinabalu, are estimated to take between 11 and 14 days.
Customers can also collect eligible online orders and selected bulky items purchased in-store at the IKEA Kuching Collection Point, operated by Hexagon Highs Transport at Jalan Demak Laut.
IKEA Kuching will operate daily from 10am to 10pm and accept cashless payments only.
To mark its arrival in Sarawak, the retailer will also hold activities for customers during its opening weekend from November 27 to 29. — The Borneo Post

Title: Former Attorney General Abdul Gani Patail dies at 71
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Former Attorney General Tan Sri Abdul Gani Patail died last night.
Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, when contacted, confirmed the news.
“He breathed his last at about 9pm,” he said.
Abdul Gani, 71, a law graduate of Universiti Malaya (UM), was the first graduate of a local university to be appointed Attorney General.
Born on Oct 6, 1955, in Lahad Datu, Sabah, he was appointed Malaysia’s eighth Attorney General on Jan 1, 2002, and served until July 2015.
He joined the Judicial and Legal Service in 1980, beginning his career as a deputy public prosecutor in Kota Kinabalu, and subsequently served as senior federal counsel in Sabah, head of the Prosecution Division and Commissioner of Law Revision.
Among the high-profile cases he handled was the prosecution of 30 individuals in connection with the Lahad Datu intrusion in February 2013.
Abdul Gani led the prosecution team in the case, which involved, among others, charges of waging war against the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
Abdul Gani’s second child, Faezul Adzra Patail, when contacted by Bernama, said his father died at Prince Court Medical Centre at 9.15pm.
“He died due to an infection and will be laid to rest at the Precinct 20 Muslim Cemetery in Putrajaya tomorrow morning (Friday),” he said. — Bernama

Title: From kampung boy to Seri Negara curator: The Khazanah scholar who made his late mother proud
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Having lost his father while still in primary school and his mother just days after his 18th birthday, Tan Chee Yong grew up facing challenges that could easily have derailed his ambitions.
Even his grandmother questioned why he wanted to dream beyond settling down in the confines of his kampung.
Instead, he pursued a Khazanah scholarship to study international relations in Britain, eventually earning a doctorate at the University of Cambridge.
Against the odds, a door opens
“When I was 18, I never expected that one day I would help restore Seri Negara, you know, the place where we signed the agreement. It all happened so fast, so weird,” Tan told Malay Mail in an interview.
Built in 1913 as an official residence and guesthouse for British administrators, Seri Negara was formerly known as Government House and later King’s House before taking its present name.
Overlooking the Perdana Botanical Gardens in Kuala Lumpur, the heritage building was where the Federation of Malaya Agreement was signed in 1948, and it is also associated with the 1957 Independence Agreement.
On December 15, 2025, Khazanah Nasional Bhd announced the completion of its restoration and the building’s reopening to the public.
Tan said he was still studying for his A-levels when he came across the Khazanah Scholarship programme through an online search.
“It’s actually rare, because not many scholarships in Malaysia offered support for studies in international relations,” he said.
Debates with his father
Tan said his interest in history began at a young age, when he would debate historical events with his father before his father passed away.
That interest grew into a fascination with international relations, diplomacy and state-building, especially after he read biographies, including one of Malaysia’s first prime minister Tunku Abdul Rahman.
“So I said then, if I want to apply to study in the UK, I want to do something that is really close to my heart, and international relations is the one.
“I like history — World War II, World War I, state-building, you know, like the Ottoman Empire, the Malay Sultanate — all the rise and fall of empires.
“I wanted to learn, so I told Khazanah that if I do it, I will do it to contribute back to the country with my expertise,” he said.
From King’s College to Cambridge
His application was successful, and he went to King’s College London in 2017 before continuing his studies at the University of Cambridge.
“That door opened me to all other doors. To Cambridge, then nation-building,” he said.
During his studies, Tan visited the UK National Archives, where he read classified documents on Malaya’s journey towards independence, including historical accounts involving Tunku Abdul Rahman and Tun Tan Cheng Lock.
The material fed into his research on Malayan state-building, which would later prove relevant to his work in Malaysia. His doctoral dissertation at Cambridge was titled “The Malayan Dilemma: Race, Power, and State Formation in Malaya”.
“I just feel like this is something that Malaysia is lacking, and I have an interest. Hopefully, with my knowledge, I can contribute to policymaking or to Malaysian diplomacy,” he said.
He said his choice of studies had become increasingly relevant amid shifting geopolitics.
“Last time, it was the traditional career path that your parents or your grandparents told you to choose, right?
“But who could have foreseen Malaysia being at the heart of all these geopolitical tensions,” he said.
Tan returned to Malaysia in mid-2025 and joined Khazanah Nasional’s research department as a research analyst. His main responsibilities include conducting high-level research on specific industries and countries to support various investment teams, including the Public Markets team.
Charting the course of Merdeka
One of Tan’s proudest professional experiences since returning has been his involvement in Project Warisan, an initiative to restore historic national landmarks in Kuala Lumpur, including Seri Negara, Carcosa and Bangunan Sultan Abdul Samad.
He said he was brought in after his superior recognised that his academic background in Malaysian history and state-building was relevant to the project.
“I came back to serve my bond, and my boss said, since this is your expertise — it so happened that we had Project Warisan — he parachuted me into it and I just got involved,” he said.
His role was not in the physical restoration of the buildings but in supporting the curation team and developing exhibition content at Seri Negara and Bangunan Sultan Abdul Samad.
At Seri Negara, he helped curate the permanent historical and cultural exhibition “Charting the Course of Merdeka”, which traces Malaya’s journey from colonial rule to independence and the formation of Malaysia across four galleries, each covering a different chapter of the country’s history.
“We managed to source and reproduce some of the photographs from the National Archives of the UK, since I studied there.
“Many of them are publicly displayed for the first time. I’m proud that Malaysians get to see them and understand a different dimension of our fight for independence.
“It’s not like Tunku just went to London so happy and declared independence. He fought for independence peacefully. Not many countries could achieve that, and it’s something Malaysians don’t really remember or understand,” he added.
He said most of his work on Seri Negara had been completed, although he remained open to contributing to similar projects in the future.
Making his mother proud
Now 28, Tan said the opportunity had also given him the chance to fulfil something he had hoped to achieve for his late mother, who had encouraged him to persevere despite the difficulties he faced growing up.
“Today, I have done something. I have made my mom proud, for that matter,” he said.
He hopes his experience will encourage young Malaysians in difficult circumstances not to give up on their ambitions.
“I know life is not easy when you are faced with all those circumstances, right? It’s easier to give up, but it’s not easy to stay on and fight for yourself.
“So you just have to believe in what you want to do, go ahead, and leave the rest to the process and trust the process.
“But if you don’t try, you will surely not get it,” he said.
Between 2006 and 2026, Yayasan Khazanah (YK) invested in developing more than 1,893 Malaysian scholars, Tan among them, expanding access to world-class education and nurturing leaders of purpose.
Its “20 Years Forward” (#YK2046) campaign marks two decades of opening doors to opportunity while looking ahead to the next 20 years of advancing Malaysia.
“They changed my life. I will be forever grateful to them,” Tan said.

Title: From remote Batang Rajang to luxury tables: Sarawak’s prized empurau commands up to RM2,500 per kg
Article:
SIBU, Nov 26 — The landing of an empurau weighing over 12 kilogrammes at the premises of Sarawak wild fish supplier Jeferry Siew Seng Kwong here proves that the species is not merely an ordinary river catch, but a luxury commodity worth tens of thousands of ringgit.
Known scientifically as Tor tambroides, the fish, which fetches RM2,000 to RM2,500 per kilogramme in the international market, continues to cement its dominance in the exclusive culinary segment.
The iconic species is now sought after by high-end restaurants, wholesalers, and the elite in Hong Kong, China, and Singapore, as well as the Peninsular Malaysia market including Kuala Lumpur, Perak, and Penang.
Behind that extraordinary price tag, the journey of the “King of the River” begins far in the remote upstream areas before passing through a chain of fishermen, suppliers, and air logistics to reach the dining tables of high-income earners.
For Jeferry, 41, the business is not merely about chasing profits through trading exotic fish, but also ensuring that every bit of hard work by local fishermen receives a fair and lucrative return.
“This empurau has its own uniqueness with fine, tender, and sweet-textured flesh as well as a fatty belly, while its special aroma comes from its natural diet as it feeds only on wild forest fruits such as engkabang and ensurai.
“A large-sized fish can fetch tens of thousands of ringgit, even enough to buy an used car, depending on its weight and the market,” he told Bernama recently.
He said the uniqueness of the empurau, which inhabits fast-flowing upstream rivers, also lies in its growth period, which takes more than 10 years.
Fresh supplies are obtained directly from fishermen’s bases in the interior such as Ulu Kapit and Baleh, with the nearly 600-kilometre Batang Rajang river basin remaining the main habitat for various high-value freshwater species.
Close cooperation with local fishermen, including Leanard Anak Lenggie and Gamas Iban from Kapit, forms the backbone of his operational stability, which demands swift action as soon as the catch is brought ashore.
He said in the wild fish trade, there is no room for any delay as timeliness is the absolute determining factor in maintaining the freshness and highest-grade quality of the empurau.
He noted that demand for the premium species usually surges ahead of festive seasons such as Christmas and Chinese New Year to be served as a special dish for families and celebratory gatherings.
Apart from empurau, Jeferry’s business premises located at Jalan Long Bridge also supply various other freshwater species including patin buah, tapah, jelawat, semah, tengadak, terubuk, sebarau, giant freshwater prawns (udang galah), ketutu, and baung.
This variety allows his business to cater to the tastes and budgets of customers from various backgrounds, rather than relying on empurau alone.
Commenting on export matters, Jeferry said shipments outside Sarawak via air freight to maintain freshness also affect the selling price, in addition to requiring permits, veterinary documents, and shipping declarations.
His experience in managing shipping as well as import-export businesses has also been an advantage in handling documentation and logistics coordination to meet customer needs.
Ahead of the 13th Sarawak State Election, the Sibu native, who will cast his ballot in the Bukit Assek state constituency, hopes the potential of the river fisheries sector, particularly high-value species like empurau, will be given due attention by elected representatives as one of the state’s economic drivers.
He said continuous support in terms of infrastructure, basic amenities, and market access is crucial to ensure Sarawak’s river produce continues to bring greater benefits to fishing communities and the rural economy.
“I believe efforts to strengthen market access, transport facilities, as well as networks between operators and suppliers also have the potential to help this sector grow, thereby ensuring Sarawak’s river produce continues to secure a place in both domestic and international premium markets,” he said.
Bukit Assek is one of two state constituencies in the Lanang parliamentary constituency, alongside Dudong, involved in the Sarawak State Election.
The Election Commission (EC) has set this Saturday (November 28) as nomination day, followed by early voting on December 8 and polling day on December 12.
Get the latest news on the 13th Sarawak State Election via https://election.bernama.com/prn/sarawak/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Cybersecurity gets its own priority in Malaysia’s new National Security Policy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today launched the National Security Policy 2026–2030, outlining Malaysia’s security priorities for the next five years, with a new strategic focus on cybersecurity and technology.
The policy takes into account changes in the geopolitical landscape and increasingly complex traditional and non-traditional security threats, aiming to strengthen the country’s preparedness against emerging challenges.
Anwar said the policy adopts a Comprehensive Security approach, covering politics, the economy, society, the environment, public safety and technology, supported by collaboration between government agencies, the private sector, academia, non-governmental organisations and the public.
“Our approach and outlook towards security threats have changed.
“We are no longer dealing solely with conventional forces or threats originating from other countries or within the region.
“This underscores the need to strengthen our cybersecurity capabilities, including investing in training and developing infrastructure to address new and increasingly unpredictable threats,” he said in his speech.
Anwar said security threats were no longer confined to conventional conflicts between countries, with cyberattacks increasingly targeting financial systems, defence networks and critical infrastructure.
“The National Security Policy takes into account the perspectives of previous policies, but I believe its strength lies in its ability to anticipate and address new issues and challenges,” he said.
He urged relevant ministries to consider setting up dedicated units to strengthen national capabilities, particularly in cybersecurity, while improving coordination between agencies.
He said these efforts must be supported by specialised expertise, including providing young officers with exposure and specialised training at leading institutions worldwide.
The National Security Policy 2026–2030 is a continuation of the previous 2021–2025 policy, which was based on the Comprehensive Security concept.
Under the latest policy, the previous nine National Security Core Values have been reorganised into 10 Strategic Focus Areas, including Sovereignty and Territorial Integrity, Sociopolitical Stability, National Cohesion, Effective Governance, Economic Resilience, Social Justice, Sustainable Development, People's Security, Security Diplomacy and Regional Cooperation, and Cybersecurity and Technology.
The last category is a new addition, reflecting the growing importance of cybersecurity and technological threats in national security planning.
The policy identifies 53 security issues, challenges and threats, which will be addressed through 30 strategies across the 10 focus areas.
Its implementation will be coordinated by the National Security Council under the Prime Minister’s Department, together with relevant ministries and agencies, with cooperation from the private sector and the public.
Monitoring mechanisms include National Security Council meetings, coordination and implementation monitoring committees, the National Security Index, security exercises and simulations, and integrated operations.
